title: Well....
text: My daughter has recently gotten her first car. I thought this would be great for her to have. Well......it's got a lot of stuff in it, but the items are pretty basic and some of them are poor quality. The kit comes in a storage bag. There are jumper cables, a safety vest, tire pressure gauge, safety triangle, ice scraper, screwdriver, tape, whistle and more. The safety vest is pretty light weight and cheap, but it works and will definitely draw attention to you if you were out changing a tire. The whistle is sturdy and decent. The safety triangle is a much better option than road flares, but it's wobbly. The rain poncho is cheap and probably only a one time use. The snow shovel is really more like an ice scraper. The tow hook is not very sturdy and it's questionable as to how strong it would be in use. Overall, it's got a lot of stuff, but it might be better to purchase better quality items that you will feel confident that will work in an emergency. We plan to do that for our daughter.

title: Nice!
text: This is a nice auto trash bag. It's lined well so it won't leak. The inner liner is removable if necessary but can be put back in it when emptied/cleaned. I like the opening on the top for putting the trash inside. It's large enough to accommodate most of my trash needs. I have it sitting on the floor between my console and lower dash of my minivan.

title: Nice Plate Frame!
text: I have never had a frame on my license plate before, but I recently got a new tag that has a lot of white space on it. It looks lost on my minivan. The frame makes a huge difference on how it looks. This was very easy to install. It's silicone and comes with everything you need to install it on your vehicle, even disposable gloves! The frame is simple and doesn't block any of the pertinent information that needs to be visible. And since it's silicone, it doesn't make any noise when going over bumps! This comes with two frames, so my husband is going to put the other one on his car.

title: Worked Well on One of Our Cars
text: My husband's license plate got all bent up in a car wash recently. I thought this would help prevent that from happening again. He drives a Honda Civic. We started to install it with the holes at the top, but that covered up the expiration date and county. My husband didn't want to get a ticket for that. So we put it up the other way with the holes at the bottom. That worked really well. The license plate is secured with screws at the top and the frame is secured at the bottom. It came with tops to cover the screws so it's all uniform looking. We planned to put the other frame on our son's car. His plate has been bent up, too. (We think our state has been using really cheap, thin metal for tags!) Unfortunately, we couldn't use it on his car. He drives a Toyota Prius. The car doesn't have screw holes at the bottom, only at the top of where the plate goes. We tried my Toyota Sienna next. Same problem. Only top holes in my car, as well. The frame works well on some cars! If you don't want information covered by the frame and use it the way we did, make sure your car can do that!

title: Easy to Set Up!
text: We recently had a trailer hitch installed on my Toyota Sienna mini van. We thought this cargo rack could come in handy, especially with our daughter moving to college this fall. From out of the box, it took my husband less than 20 minutes to assemble. He used a socket set instead of the tools provided, which he recommends to anyone getting this. Once it was put together, it didn't take long to set it up on the van's hitch. It does require a wrench for installing it on the hitch, so make sure you take one with you just in case. There's a sleeve inside the bar that attaches to the hitch. The first time we tried hooking it up, the sleeve had slipped out a little, so we could not get the bolt to screw in because the threads weren't lined up properly. Once we discovered that, we were more careful when sliding it on to the hitch so the sleeve wouldn't slide out and we were able to get it in correctly. The hitch we have is close to the ground. This angles up a little so it leaves adequate clearance. My husband drove it around the neighborhood a few times and didn't notice any rattling or other noises, and it seemed to drive smoothly. The rack is pretty sturdy and well made. It did get scratched up a little during assembly though. Overall, we're quite pleased with it and better yet, we don't think we'll need to rent a trailer to move our daughter into her dorm. I think between this and the space in the van, we'll be good.

title: Heavy duty
text:
I got tired of those "stick" tire pressure gauges breaking and of wondering whether they're accurate or not. For less than ten bucks this is good:

PROS: Heavy duty; either side of the connector works so can use at different angles; checked it against a friend's expensive air compressor gauge and it's accurate; bleeder valve lets out air down to PSI you want; round part is encased in rubber.

CONS: Turns a one-handed job (with the stick gauge) into a two-handed job; takes up more space in a glove compartment.

Press the connector onto the tire and it pressurizes the gauge to the PSI. Then the gauge holds the reading until you press the bleeder valve on the side. I fill my tires to ~35 PSI on a 12-volt portable air compressor, then use this and bleed it down to 30. Easy every time.

title: Perfect Fit, Easy to Manage
text:
We purchased two sets of front floor liners, one for a Ford Escape and the other for a Jeep Patriot. The installation in the Jeep turned out to be much more satisfactory for the following reasons: (1) the liners are much more FLEXIBLE than the ones we received for the Escape; and (2) the Jeep uses a simple hook to hold the driver's side carpet in place. The design of the liner on the driver's side easily accommodates the hook. (See my companion review of the liners for a Ford Escape.)

Because of the flexibility of the liners and the interior design of the Jeep, it appears that the liners will be easily removable should they contain liquid or debris. They will readily go "straight up and out" of the vehicle should the need arise.

The installation of the liners in the Jeep turned out to be a much more satisfying experience than for the Escape. The liners for the Jeep give a much better measure of this product. You should be very happy, as we are, if you buy these liners for your Jeep Patriot!

title: Keeps Your Vehicle Clean (Updated June 2013)
text:
These liners cover the front carpet for both the driver and passenger sides. They are very sturdy and help to trap whatever would have wound up on your interior carpeting. They fit snugly. All very good so far.

The Ford Escape has two grommets (plastic) that normally hold the carpet in place. To install the liners, you must remove the carpet, which is easy to do. This leaves the two grommets exposed. Now the liner does have grommet holes which are supposed to match up with and fit over the two grommets. This is where matters go slightly awry: the liners that I received for the Escape are VERY stiff, so it is not very easy to position the liner holes over the grommets -- esp. the grommet farther in. I was not able to get the grommets into the holes of the liner. The holes seem a tad small. It does not seem to matter, because the liner fits very snugly and does not seem to move around at all. Since there are no grommets on the passenger front carpeting, there is no issue on the passenger side.

Because the liners I received are so stiff, I am not quite sure how easy it will be to lift the liners out and dispose of any liquid that might accumulate (e.g. snow, coffee spills, and the like). There is the possibility that in trying to remove these liners, the liquid could wind up all over the remaining layer of carpet. It does not seem that the liners will easily go "straight up and out" because of the inside dimensions of the Escape and the size of the liners.

All in all I am glad we bought them, because they are better than the alternative -- messy carpets. The liners are well made and they look good in the vehicle. I just wish they were a bit more flexible for the reasons outlined above.

All the while, the car was still sitting in my driveway - according to the device.  I've had multiple conversations with both AT&T and Agnik (the car connection 2.0 people) and finally got an answer that the device is faulty, and I should request a replacement.  I was given the phone number for Audiovox to request an RMA and nobody EVER answers that phone number, regardless of day of the week OR time of day.  I absolutely don't believe it's the device though, since it is obviously getting a good connection and everything, and a few minutes on the car connection 2.0 website leads anyone to believe it's absolutely agnik side problem.  I swear it's like that website is hosted on a 14.4 modem and changes are almost impossible to make.  Right now, the website and the app are showing completely different information because they're not syncing up.  My contract on the device is up here in a few months. title: Pump Quits Without Warning After 2-3 Months
text:
This IDEAWORKS JB4840 SIERRA TOOLS JB5684 BATTERY OPERATED LIQUID TRANSFER PUMP is extremely fast and efficient for pumping water–until it simply stops working. This has happened with all three (3) of my pumps.

The first time, I thought that the malfunction was my fault, because I had been careless about turning the pump upside down. This allows water to enter the battery compartment, so it seemed reasonable that the pump might quit due to wet connectors. After all, the instructions warn you NOT to turn the pump upside down.

The second time, I was extremely careful about keeping the pump upright. It worked longer than the first pump, but quit unexpectedly–in the middle of a job–after a few months.

The third time, the pump worked exactly like the second pump. I loved using these pumps for emptying water out of my Aerogardens, but they have to be replaced far too often. Apparently there is something wrong with the design or quality control.

The pumps cost too much (about $18.50 on Amazon) to be replaced every few months. If you decide to take a chance on this product, be sure that you have a backup siphon available to use when it quits on you.

title: Purchased to Carry in Car’s Trunk for Emergencies
text:
I ordered this FOSEAL PORTABLE AIR COMPRESSOR PUMP (12V DC, 150 PSI, Auto Shut-off; with Emergency Led Light & Long Cable; Red) to carry in the trunk of my Honda Accord for emergencies. I don’t want to repeat an incident where my car’s “Low Tire Pressure" warning light came on when I was far from any source of compressed air. (I do forget to check the tire pressure regularly.)

It’s amazing to me that this lightweight box can be an air compressor--and that it can work from an automobile’s accessory power socket. Inflating a tire with this takes only a few minutes. You just connect the pump to the accessory socket and to the tire. Then you set the desired air pressure, press the “On” button, and wait while the pump inflates the tire. The pump turns off automatically when the preset air pressure is reached.

The recommended air pressure for your tires is usually found on a sticker placed where you can read it if you open the door on the driver’s side. My first choice in a tire inflator is the [[ASIN:B015VXWZ9O JACO SmartPro Digital Tire Inflator]], but it is currently unavailable (apparently the manufacturer is readying a new model).

A portable tire inflator like this one is much easier to use than an air hose at a gasoline station. (And you don't have someone breathing down your neck, waiting to use the air hose, either.)

I haven’t owned the Foseal Air Compressor Pump for long enough to know how reliable it is, or how long it will last.

title: 12.5” Swivel Seat Is Too Small for Bucket Seat of Honda Accord
text:
This HEALTHSMART SWIVEL SEAT CUSHION (Black with Red Stripe, 12.5 Inches in Diameter) works fine as a swivel cushion for my little black folding stool; it does NOT work as a swivel cushion in the passenger-side bucket seat of my Honda Accord. Although it appears to fit the Accord’s bucket seat, it sinks down into the middle of the seat, and the flared sides of the seat prevent the cushion from swiveling.

What does work in the Accord’s bucket seat is a larger [[ASIN:B003DLXEA6 16-inch diameter Medline swivel cushion]]. The larger swivel cushion sits atop the flared sides of the bucket seat, and the cushion is able to swivel. The swivel cushion is extremely helpful to my disabled husband, when he gets in and out of the car.

The 12.5” striped HealthSmart swivel seat is a “Vivi” brand swivel seat, made in China, and “manufactured for HealthSmart International”. It seems to be reasonably well made, and the cover is machine washable. Obviously the red-and-black swivel seat is NOT a good match for the ivory upholstery of my car, but that wouldn’t matter if the small cushion were able to swivel.

In my experience, the plastic swivel portion of this type of cushion always wears out over time. The person’s weight causes the connection between the plastic swivel part and the cushion to break, or else the plastic swivel portion cracks. You can expect to have to replace any regularly-used swivel cushion from time to time.

title: Stopped Working.  Signal-Blocking Pouch Protects Cars With Keyless Entry Systems
text:
UPDATE: One year later, I retested this item, and it has stopped working. My car starts even though the car key fob is inside the Faraday bag. Another of these, purchased at the same time but used only to shield a second car key fob stored in a drawer, is still blocking the fob signal (so that my car won't start.) Star rating downgraded from 5 stars to 1 star, because of lack of durability and need to regularly retest for effectiveness.

This UPGRADED TICONN PREMIUM FARADAY BAG FOR KEY FOB (2 Pack) completely blocks the signal from my 2019 Honda Accord key fob. When the transmitter is inside the bag, and inside the car, the car absolutely will NOT start. Just make sure that you place the fob in the BACK pocket (the one with the white lining). The front pocket does NOT block the signal.

Keyless car entry systems (like those on the newer Hondas) make the cars that are equipped with them much harder to steal. However, thieves with sophisticated tech knowledge and equipment can enter or steal these cars by (1) hacking the fobs with signal boosting software, or (2) capturing the fob signal as the driver walks away, using special equipment developed by auto manufacturers.

If you always store your fob inside a metal box or a signal-blocking pouch like this one, you are protected from these kinds of thieves. (You definitely need to store the fob inside the pouch even when the fob is inside your home.) Other reviewers say that signal-blocking pouches stop working after a time, so be sure to test the pouch every so often to verify that it’s still working.

This pouch is large enough to easily store my Honda fob and an attached keychain charm. There’s room left over.

text:
This DIEHARD 19" BEAM WIPER BLADE (1 Pack) fits the passenger side of my 2003 Honda Civic. It’s a very good wiper blade, though I generally prefer conventional wiper blades to beam-style wiper blades. (A beam-style blade consists of a single long, heavy strip of rubber; it’s flexible, and conforms to the exact shape of the windshield surface. However, in my experience, because a beam-style blade constantly flexes a bit while in use, the blade starts streaking sooner with age.)

I replace my Honda’s wiper blades at least once a year, because the car is parked outdoors (in California). DieHard wiper blades stand up well in this situation, where the blades are exposed to a lot of sun.

Be sure to take advantage of Amazon’s feature that lets you “register” your car. You only need to do this once, and afterwards the web site will automatically tell you whether an automobile part that you’re looking at (like this 19” blade) will fit your car. The feature is extremely useful when you need two different lengths of wiper blade for your car’s windshield.

The tea tree oil has a pleasant odor that masks or eliminates unwanted odors. I can now stop using air freshener stick-ups inside the garbage can--they're expensive and only marginally effective against garbage odors.

In my experience, Star Brite products do a great job on all tough-to-clean items--the [[ASIN:B01KY0II8G Extreme Clean product]] made me a Star Brite convert for life. It’s the only thing that has ever worked to periodically clean a metal commode frame that rusts.

Unfortunately, my Star Brite Tea Tree Oil arrived with a defective sprayer. It would pump up liquid, but nothing came out of the nozzle. (Yes, I opened the sprayer by pushing the tab down and turning the nozzle to “On”.) The oil works with an ordinary sprayer--I had one available--but my substitute doesn’t produce a spray that is fine enough for use as a room air freshener.

title: Perfect for Illuminating Craft, Hobby Projects
text:
This LIGHT-N-CARRY LNCMINI MANTIS RECHARGEABLE COB LED WORK LIGHT is small, but it produces a lot of light. The stand (with or without the magnet) allows you to direct a steady light to a specific area on your desktop, workbench, or working repair scene (e.g., undersink plumbing). The light has a very small footprint (taking up a negligible amount of surface work space), and fits into tight working areas. It’s very lightweight and portable (there’s a pocket clip).

This light is perfect for illuminating craft and hobby projects. I love it for assembling LEGO models. The focused beam (like a flashlight) lets me quickly locate dropped bricks (they bounce to the oddest places!). The steady beam (low or high setting) lights up the assembly instructions (especially the brick illustrations printed in dark blue or black ink). The light itself takes up minimal space on my worktable.

Charging takes a while, but the light runs to as much as four hours on a full charge, and it holds the charge. A braided charging cable and AC adapter is included. A row of four LED lights (on the side with the pocket clip) keeps you informed about the charge level.

title: It'll Get You There . . . or Close to There
text:
There are three big reasons why I'm not crazy about my TomTom VIA 1405TM GPS navigator. First, it often plots routes requiring a lot of extra driving around, even after I've installed the latest maps. Second, the touch screen isn't very sensitive, so that an instruction to "tap" really means "press and hold". Third, the on-screen navigation displays are kind of clunky, so that extra "taps" are needed to cancel operations, select operations, and get traffic information.

ROUTES. The routes are something of a problem. A couple of actual examples: (1) When I asked for a route from one store to a nearby Safeway store (in a small shopping center), the TomTom ignored a traffic signal that allowed a left turn into the shopping center's parking lot, and routed me around several extra blocks so that I could make a right turn into the same parking lot. (2) When I intentionally went off route on my way home, the TomTom failed to adjust to my alternate, non-freeway route, and kept giving instructions for returning to the original, freeway route that was now far out of my way. It was only when I was very close to home that the instructions adjusted to take me home along the alternate route.

VOICE INSTRUCTIONS. Closely related to the routes issue is the quality of the voice instructions. Usually these tell you to prepare for turns, and to make turns, in plenty of time. However, on the freeway the voice instructions do not tell you to get out of forced-exit lanes (although the driving map shows the correct lanes), and they frequently tell you to "keep left" when all you need to do is continue on down the freeway. Maybe the voice is worried that you'll take the next exit ramp? Also, the voice instructions frequently say that you've reached your destination when your destination is only close by (perhaps a half block ahead). Worse, when you go off route by turning into a parking lot before you've reached the plotted end of your route--a good idea, since your plotted destination is often beyond the last parking lot entrance--the voice instructions become very confusing as they attempt to direct you back to the plotted route.

TOUCH SCREEN. The sensitivity of the touch screen is adequate for general navigation and plotting of routes. However, because a "tap" isn't enough, it's unwise to attempt these operations while you're driving, unless you're stopped in traffic. The main issue here, is that you can only get "traffic incident" and "delay" information by touching and holding the appropriate spot on your 3D route screen, so you'll be wanting to check this when driving. (Live traffic information is available on this model when your device is plugged into your car's power or cigarette-lighter socket).

NAVIGATION MENUS. The home screen has a "drive to" option that lets you choose a favorite, find a point of interest, or program a new address. But when you choose a location and route, you must touch the "Done" button at the lower right to reach the 3D driving map. There are many screens that require you to hit "Done" or "Back" to go elsewhere. Having to back out of screens is not only clunky, it's unsafe when you're driving (because you have to keep pressing and holding a spot on the small screen). Some nice menu features are (1) the Zoom buttons for the maps (but not as useful as they might be because the lack of screen sensitivity makes them unavailable, as a practical matter, when you're driving); (2) the "exclude part of route" option (e.g., exclude the freeway) that enables you to plot an alternative to the default route ("fastest" is the factory default setting); and (3) the "route planning" options for route types (fastest, shortest, bicycle, walking), and ferries, unpaved roads, etc. A not-so-nice feature is the ease with which you can inadvertently change your Home address or a Favorite address to something that's programmed in that isn't the correct address.

SETTING UP. Setting up the device was a little confusing for me. My Win7 computer didn't recognize it at first, although my WinXP computer recognized it right away. Perhaps the device needed some charging, perhaps it needed to be turned on. I've discovered that it may be necessary to press the "on" button several times, or to press and hold the button, to turn it on. (There's a convenient setting available that will turn the device on and off automatically when you plug it into a power source, but this is not the factory default setting.) Once you have the device plugged in, you need to go to TomTom's "get started" web site to download whatever new software and maps are available. You will have to create an account, so that you can work from "My TomTom". As I was figuring all this out, the software gave conflicting messages by saying that the device was up to date when it wasn't. Finally I learned that the TomTom device will show a "do not disconnect" warning when it is actually doing an update.

BATTERY LIFE. The TomTom VIA 1405TM display depletes the battery's charge quickly if the device is not connected to a power source (there are battery-saving options that will help with this a little). When you are driving, you will want to plug it into the car's power socket (an adapter is included, which also enables live traffic information on this model). In addition, you can charge the battery with the included USB cable by plugging the device into your computer or into a USB wall plug adapter (e.g., [[ASIN:B006GWO5WK Amazon Kindle PowerFast]]). Because of the short battery life, you will probably need a powerpack (e.g., [[ASIN:B007ZQJ5XU Incredicharge I-8800 Backup Battery Charger]]) if you plan to use this device for bicycling, walking, or bus routes. The battery icon appears on the 3D map (drive a route) display when the device is disconnected from any power source, but not otherwise.

LOCKING-SUCTION-CUP MOUNT. The device is permanently attached to a locking-suction-cup mount. You can attach the mount to your car's windshield with the suction cup, or attach the mount to the included adhesive disk (which you attach to your dashboard). Because I don't trust suction cups on windshields, and don't like having a permanent GPS mount showing in my car, I attached the mount to a portable [[ASIN:B0051FWA7U AmazonBasics GPS Dashboard Mount for TomTom]]. When locked, the suction-cup mount seems to hold quite firmly.

COMPARISON TO OTHER NAVIGATION DEVICES. The only other GPS navigation device that I own is the Verizon Navigator feature on my cell phone ($1.99 a month discounted in a special offer; regular price $4.99 a month). I think that the Verizon Navigator is quite a bit better than the dedicated TomTom VIA 1405TM device. The Verizon routes are direct (without including unnecessary extra blocks of driving); the information on bus, walking, and other alternate routes is more accessible; there is better information on nearby points of interest that are possible destinations; the navigator warns me when I've gone off route, and plots a new, efficient route immediately; the traffic lanes change color in the Navigator display to show congestion when traffic delay information is available; the voice commands are generally clearer; and the onscreen navigation is more intuitive. Although this TomTom VIA 1405TM model includes lifetime maps (you must activate the feature, using a code provided in the box), it will take many months of using Verizon Navigator before the cost of the feature will equal the cost of the dedicated TomTom GPS device. Thus a navigator app may be a better choice if you own a smartphone.

If you don't own a smartphone, the TomTom VIA 1405TM should work for you, once you get familiar with the updating, the display screens, the route plotting, and the lingo of the voice instructions. The device will reliably direct you to your destination, or at least to a point close to your destination. Because the TomTom VIA 1405TM works reasonably well as a GPS navigator, but has its drawbacks, I rate it at 3 stars ("It's OK" on the official Amazon scale).

title: Extreme Facial Closeups Only
text:
At 20X magnification, the ZADRO 20X SPOT MIRROR provides extreme facial closeups. It's not really a makeup mirror, although it's great for tweezing eyebrows (and even eyelashes if you're careful), because you can see to grip individual hairs with your tweezers. I bought this small mirror to be able to inspect sun-damaged skin on my nose and face, in order to identify any tiny, possibly precancerous skin lesions that should be removed by my dermatologist if they should start to exhibit changes. For this purpose, the 20X magnification is perfect.

To use this mirror, you need to hold it close to your eyes and look straight into it. Otherwise you can't see a focused image. Thus it's a mirror with very limited use. For general purposes (e.g., applying eye makeup), a magnifying mirror with 5X magnification is a much better choice, because the 5X mirror will show a larger area of your face.

title: Three Gaskets, One Spring, for Repair of Leifheit Cherrymat
text:
The [[ASIN:B001MSYWQW Leifheit Cherrymat]] is great for pitting large quantities of fresh cherries, but it's somewhat fragile. The metal rod that punches the pits out of the cherries can damage a misaligned rubber gasket, or the rubber gasket can simply wear out. Apparently the spring (in the handle) that powers the punch rod can also wear out.

This Cherrymat repair kit includes three (3) replacement rubber gaskets, and one (1) replacement spring for the handle--exactly as pictured in the product photo. I'm not pleased that I needed a Cherrymat repair kit so soon, but I'm very pleased that a repair kit is available.

This repair kit ensures that I'll have a "production" cherry pitter available for home use during the full cherry season (after I damaged one of the two gaskets that came with the pitter). The Cherrymat has spoiled me, because I can prepare whole bowls of stemmed, pitted cherries in advance, and have the cherries ready for a pure, delightful eating experience.

title: Nice kit that should be in your car
text:
I got this after my car battery died and I realized my jumper cables had a tear and wouldn't work. While it probably makes sense to have a set of jumper cables just in case this doesn't work, this is the self-contained solution to jump your battery.

It comes with a nice carry case to keep everything organized too. The display on the unit shows that battery level, which is super useful when determining when you should charge. My big question is how long the unit will hold charge without being used/charged. Since the units last full charge a month ago,the battery is still at 100% (it's been kept at room temp; I'm not sure how a cold climate would affect this).

It's also really nice that you can use this to charge other electronics (phone, etc.) in the case of a pinch (though to be honest, just get a car adapter).I would recommend keeping this solely for jumping the battery if needed.

The jumper cables feel plasticky and the battery unit itself has a nice heft, but also has a little plastic feeling. That said, it works perfectly, so I won't deduct any stars for it.

I've been really impressed with this and would definitely recommend it (in addition to a set of actual jumper cables just in case!)

title: Contains two full-size one-piece bucket seat covers; video is wrong; description was wrong
text:
When I ordered this, the description said this was leather and the video shows the seat cover in two pieces. As a result, I understood that this was for one seat (a top and bottom). However, this is for two seats, which is great and a better deal.

I have a 2006 Toyota Camry Solara Convertible with heated seats. Both of my front seats are worn so this is perfect for covering the tiny tears in the leather. The installation is pretty simple to figure out after watching the video. I first put the two center chucks into the crease of the seat. I am not able to pull them through on my car because the back is covered, so I have to secure it by feel. I then put the hood over the headrest, and finally hooked the hooks under my seat.

There are four negatives that I found. First, this buckles a bit on the top because my headrest is not all the way up. However, it does not affect performance. Second, this covers the seat belt strap (see photo), so that cannot be used. Third, it also covers the seat belt connector, so I have to tuck the material underneath. Fourth, the clip that hooks on the bottom, came off the elastic. I had to thread that back on.

This feels very comfortable to sit on and does not budge. It also covers more of the seat than my previous [[ASIN:B08T235CC8 cover]] but that cover did not buckle or hide my seat belt items.

The current price of $69.99 comes to $35 per cover which I feel is competitively priced. Had the Amazon site not lied about this being leather (which it now corrected), if it were not misleading about being two separate pieces, and there were no negatives, this would have gotten 5 stars.

title: Powerful enough to jump start cars and some trucks and RVs; HEAVY
text:
This review is for the Schumacher DSR ProSeries DSR 141G 2000A 12V Jump Starter that is made in Mexico.

I have been carrying a jump starter in my vehicle since the 1990’s because I got tired of trying to find someone who would give me a jump with my booster cables every time I was stranded in a parking lot away from home. I used to own a car where the standard form of transportation was a tow. Thankfully those days are over.

This is my eighth jump starter and I ordered this because my heavy duty one that I got in June of 2017 is at the end of its life. My first two were an AC Delco and another one whose name escapes me. I also currently own a [[ASIN:B06XD6XBCM DEWALT DXAEJ14 Digital Portable Power Station Jump Starter 1400 Peak with 700 Instant Amps and 120 PSI Digital Air Compressor and two 3.1A USB Ports]] and am on my second [[ASIN:B000XQ9MGE Jump-N-Carry JNC300XL 900 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] (which is great for small tasks and jumping small cars). I also previously owned two of [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. Personally, the Jump-N-Carry (JNC) brand is my favorite and they are the ones (both the JNC300XL and JNCAIR 1700) I would carry with me all the time if I did not order this one.

Over the last 10 years I regularly carry two jump starters in my trunk. One acts as a backup (that is the JNC300XL) and is available to also charge a cell or GPS or dash cam and the other is heavy like this one and can jump several vehicles at a time in any weather.

With regard to this unit, this should be charged a minimum of 36 hours to a maximum of 48 hours before first use. It should also be re-charged every month after that. Mine arrived fully charged. This is a powerful 2000 AMPS, which is really designed to jump multiple cars, some trucks, or some commercial vehicles or some RVs in all climates without having to recharge after the first use. I personally like to have a powerful unit with me because I want to be able to get more than one jump out of it before I recharge. I’ve charged both my boyfriend’s and my girlfriend’s cars in the past with my JNC without having to recharge for a couple of months. Since I do not have a dead battery, I have not used this Schumacher to jump a car yet. However, I tested the 12V port and it worked flawlessly. I trust that this will work well to jumpstart a car or truck several times over.

Therefore, this is designed for jump starting only with the ability to charge a 12V appliance like a cell phone, GPS, dash cam, portable air compressor, 12V car vacuum, etc. There are a couple of things missing on this unit at this price point that I would have liked to have. I would have loved the addition of an air compressor and a light. This Schumacher is comparable to the [[ASIN:B01GQDBNWS JNC770R 1700 Peak Amp]] except this one has 300 more AMPS. Note that my [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 favorite jumpstart]] can sometimes be purchased for under $160 when it goes on sale. Therefore, when I say “at this price point,” I’m comparing the sale price of my favorite to the regular price of this one.

The recommended recharging time for this one is every month. For the JNC, the recommended recharge is every three months, which I like better.

In summary, this is an excellent jump starter. I have faith this will work to jump a battery even though I did not have a dead battery to test this on. In addition, the 12V port is great for charging cell phones or operating a portable air compressor. This unit is heavy and is designed for jump starting cars and some trucks, RVs, or commercial vehicles. It will be a workhorse for that purpose when paired with the appropriate vehicle. The current price of $152.99 is competitively priced. If one also needs an air compressor, then I suggest either the JNC or Dewalt I mentioned above. The Dewalt even has two USB ports. However, I just happen to love the JNC brand. It all comes down to one’s needs. If I was not so in love with the JNC, this unit would have received 5 stars from me. PS - I love the limited edition green color!

title: Not manufactured to the standards of my Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 & missing a 12 volt DC outlet but lights are excellent
text:
This is my fifth jump starter. Two jump starters from the past wore out; one of which was an AC Delco. I currently have two others that still work. A [[ASIN:B000XQ9MGE Jump-N-Carry JNC300XL 900 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] (which is great for small tasks and jumping small cars) and [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. Personally, the Jump-N-Carry (JNC) brand is my favorite over the previous two brands I tried and over this DeWalt.

I always carry two jump starters with me in case I ever have to jump start my car or put air in my tires. I also use the ones I currently own for when I need an another DC outlet to power an extra GPS or other 12V accessory. My JNC300XL is dying so, I got this DeWalt as a backup to that.

This DeWalt is comparable in power to the [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]]. The unit is also very heavy like the JNCAIAR 1700. Even though this appears to arrive 100% charged, I charged it for 40 hours before first use as the manual recommends. This contains a lead-acid battery, so it needs periodic charging as heavy discharges between recharges will cause loss of battery life.

The unit has:
- A backlit LCD screen
- An air compressor with hose (with ability to decrease or increase pressure and stop at a set PSI rating)
- Two 5V USB Ports
- An alternator check button (manual instructions must be followed)
- Jumper clamps for jump starting a battery
- Build-in 120 Volt AC Charger (NOTE that the AC cord is NOT provided. I use a cord similar to this [[ASIN:B007T1UUOY Calrad 55-788 18 AWG AC Extension Cord, Black, 6 Inches]])
- Two banks of three LED lights that are very bright; this is my most favorite feature
- Also supplied are a 12 Volt DC Charging Adapter and a nozzle adapter for the air hose

In addition, it comes with a one-year limited warranty.

However, I am disappointed that this unit DOES NOT have a DC outlet to power 12 volt accessories. Unless I buy some sort of converter like [[ASIN:B01J67JIOQ ARECORD USB A Male to 12V Car Cigarette Lighter Socket Female Converter]], I cannot power my GPS or attach any other 12V accessory like a car vacuum cleaner to this unit. Since I already have chargers for my phone that plug into my car lighter, I don't really need the individual USB ports because if this unit had a DC outlet, I can always use the car charger instead.

Besides this, my biggest disappointment is in the quality standard of the booster cables. As you can see from the attached pictures, both the positive and negative cables have exposed wiring. Appearance-wise this looks dangerous; it also looks sloppy but I'm more concerned about the danger. I still plan to use this unit as a backup when one of my JNC's fail; however, due to the exposed wiring (that none of my past and present jump starters have ever had) and the lack of DC outlet, this is not a unit I would buy.

I am partial to the quality of the JNC and if one is looking for a powerful jump start, my recommendation is to consider the [[ASIN:B000KPU8F2 Jump-N-Carry JNCAIR 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter with Air Compressor]] or the [[ASIN:B000JFJLP6 Jump-N-Carry JNC660 1700 Peak Amp 12V Jump Starter]] first. For charging small passenger vehicles, then the lower end JNC300XL works fine and a heavy unit like the JNCAir 1700 or this DeWalt is not needed. However, the JNC300XL has a low quality light and does not have an air compressor but if one has an external 12V air compressor like I do, that unit will power it with its internal DC outlet. Besides the JNC300XL is extremely portable and compact and the one unit I had for years prior to buying the JNCAIR 1700 on sale.

title: The standard-size cover is almost perfect for my car but the magnets need to be much stronger
text:
I purchased the standard size cover and it is just barely perfect for my 2006 Toyota Camry Solara Convertible. I have two peek-a-book holes on each side of the top of the windshield with this size so I probably should have purchased the larger size. However, since my car is a convertible, I only have the top part of the windshield frame against which I can place the top magnets. Other vehicles at least have the roof, which I do not.

The cover does adhere snugly and does keep the ice and frost off my windshield. It's both easy to affix to the car and easy to remove. One shake of the cover dislodges any ice crystals that have formed. Although the plastic is very thin it still does the job. My only complaint it that the magnets are not strong enough.

During mildly to very windy days, the top part of the cover keeps pulling away from my car and folding over so that 30% of my windshield is exposed. One day I re-seated it six times and finally gave up. However, when there's little or no wind it works like a charm.

UPDATE February 23, 2015: Branden Conn, owner of Owner Apex Automotive, contacted me about the magnet issue. They had first contacted me before I even posted a review to ask how I liked this cover. I replied and then posted my review. He has since written back and below is his response about the magnets.

"Our magnets are the strength that they are in order to prevent scuffing and scratching of the vehicle's paint. On windshield covers, if the magnets holds on too strongly, the wind will move it while it's attached and the magnet itself or the grit/dirt between the magnet and the car acts as an abrasive which scratches the paint. Our magnets break away in a high wind before that damage can occur.

With that said we are always trying to find that perfect balance between the two (having a firm attachment and avoiding scuffing) so it is great to hear this feedback and I will pass it on to our design team so we can look into adjusting magnet strength."

UPDATE March 2, 2015 - I put this cover on before a snowstorm I had last night. Although the cover stayed in place, I would not do this again. When I went to remove the cover this morning, it was like peeling tape off my windshield and car because ice had formed underneath the cover. There was probably some melting going on that seeped under the cover which caused this. However, this is excellent for keeping frost off the windshield, I just can't recommend keeping it on if it's going to snow.

title: Degreaser worked exceptionally well for my use
text:
I originally requested this product for review because I wanted to remove gunk and grease that some door edge guard left on my car doors. However, after I got the product, the instructions said not to use on motorcycles or glass and that some surfaces like aluminum alloys, plastic or painted surfaces are inherently sensitive to alkaline cleaners.

I called technical support at the company and was told to definitely not use it on the painted surface of my car because the technician felt it would surely damage the paint or finish. In fact he recommended a certain Spray 9 degreaser for that job. I then asked him if I could use it on plastics (even though it says some plastics might be sensitive). He did say that because there were so many plastics on the market, I would have to spot test it to see.

Therefore, I decided to take a chance and try this cleaner on a plastic grain shovel I have. I use this shovel for snow and was told by well-meaning neighbors to grease it up so the snow would fall off easily (that never worked). For two winters, I tried different greases on the shovel that caused such severe discoloration and tackiness that no amount of dawn, soap and water, or scrubbing with an abrasive sponge would clean. I had given up on this shovel because it had so much grease and I felt it would never be clean again.

I decided to spot test Grez-Off on the bottom of this shovel and noticing there was no bad reaction I sprayed the entire shovel and immediately used a light sponge to wipe (no hard rubbing required) and then rinse off the grease using a garden hose. The shovel looks brand new. I am actually shocked at how exceptionally well this grease came off when at the end of two winters I've tried to clean it with absolutely no success and lots strenuous scrubbing.

Of course, I followed the instructions on the back of the product precisely and because of these warnings I safely used the product outside. According to the instructions, Grez-Off is a powerful biodegradable degreaser that requires:
- the application surface to be cool
- the solution should be sprayed on full strength allowing it to penetrate the grease but NEVER allowing it to dry
- the surface should be immediately rinsed with water
- the operator should not inhale and protective gloves should be used

By following the above instructions, I was able to use this product safely with exceptional results so I consider this a five-star degreaser for certain applications.

title: Better than most ice scrapers but still falls short of perfection
text:
I purchased the two-pack of these because I was tired of the different plastic ice scrapers I had that didn't do a good job on hard ice.

From September to April I have to scrap my car windows almost daily. This scraper is one of the better tools because there are three different scraping positions. You can scrape in the position shown (although I had trouble keeping it in that position), you can fold the two larger blades back to expose only the smaller blade, or you can fold all the blades in front for a stronger scraping action (although sometimes the ice gets caught between the different blades forcing them to separate a bit which means you need to clear the ice to continue).

This is the best scraper I used so far because it scrapes away thicker ice easily when in the reinforced position (with all blades out front). It also works well, but not great, to dislodge the thick concrete ice I get on my windshield.

I feel this product could be improved by making the blades stronger and have a locking mechanism that keeps the blades in the "stand-like" position (like shown in picture) and in the reinforced position (with all blades out front). Because the blades are slightly pliable and not as firm as a thick steel knife, scraping away ice is still not as easy as wiping away snow from a windshield but it is a whole lot better with this tool. One other issue I found is that the blade only scrapes half of its length (so if you use the small blade only what's in the center gets scraped away, meaning you'll have more passes).

However, this is still a worthwhile purchase for me because it's a lot easier to scrape away the ice with this tool than any other scraper I tried before.

title: States set is compatible with our car- But it isn’t!!
text:
After double checking and being certain this universal seat cover set was listed to fit our specific car, make and model- we ordered… Only problem was- it didn’t fit!!
Just purchasing our newly licensed son a used vehicle that is as old is he is.. ouch! And of course, you might imagine- the leather has seen better days! In a hope to spruce up the interior we ordered Turismo car seat covers to do the job…

Following instructions- we removed headrests and hit the first few snags in just the front 2 covers alone..

1. all of the buttons for seat control will be inaccessible if using the covers. There is no cut out or accommodation to work around them. Moving past this for a minute..

2. we were next confronted by the interior movable arm rest!! There is no way to fit arm rest under seat cover and still have usability.. Covers had no cut out or opening to slip arm rest through..??? Basically we lost 2 important features just trying to apply the front 2 covers.

Onto the split bench in back-

3. we lost usability of middle console. It is covered under fabric with no accommodation cut into material to move up/down.. OR, still have access to use the ski pass thru to the trunk.. But, deal breaker was

4. built in seatbelts! Yes, there are openings for the bottom clip mechanism.. but we lose the shoulder straps built into the seat itself…

We purchased expecting not to lose features bc of stated compatibility with our car. We could tolerate a few creature comforts being eliminated however not safety needs.

Material is quite thin… I’m sure that is a must to be compatible with airbag requirements. They have A LOT of stretchability… even a bit too much! Not a lot of shape is held when on- they felt/fit/looked a bit baggy. I’m sure it’s hard to be universal to all shapes and sizes thus, causing a fit like a glove result to be missing! Material is smooth and not itchy or irritable- each piece comes with several hooks to secure tightly under seat, only we never got that far! Once obstacles had safety issue- we had to remove.

For a price point of $35… It was a good try that fell short. If ordering, attempt placement right away so if these do not fit.. you can rectify. It would be helpful if compatibility guide was more accurate. Hoping info can help make your decision- stay safe everyone!

title: Has its perks but, not as a “real” bucket!!
text:
Great in theory and will come through in a pinch but… Let’s just call it what it is-? Foldable soft sided bucket!! Translation: it is an inverted scoop shape item that can “in theory contain water!!”

But, if you also view the photos… You’ll see, the outer brim does not like to hold it shape, at least when it’s empty of water! The price point of under $10 its spot on!! So, I don’t think anyone would be truly disappointed with what this can offer you. But, for my specific need- car wash “bucket” it’s not the ideal solution. I hope this info can help your decision.. feel free to let me know!

title: Car fanatic husband loves ceramic shine.. just look at photo!!
text:
Officially, a moment of silence please! This is the first time for me submitting photos with a review,
as I’ve lack the skills to do so until now, consider it mastered! ! Shss.. Hmmm... ok, moment over!!

The instigator behind the photo and the order, was my husband.. he said, ”people won’t believe this product- which means- a photo op is a Must..!!!” He said people NEED to see the craziness of this shine (observe in photo) and it’s all in thanks to Turtle Wax Hybrid Ceramic Wax. said it’s truly, one of the best waxes he’s ever seen- and I’m telling you, he is a car washing fanatic- (loves cars but, fanatical about washing them!) albeit, this love is limited to washing the outside of the car only.. (and Yes! That drives me crazy… But, its a whole other story.. or, therapy session needed!) If you see in images, the results speak can for themself- The swanky shiny look was achieved by using turtle wax on a newly washed car. All you need to apply, is a soft micro fiber cloth and a minimal amount of elbow grease!

My husband is NOT 100% partial or loyal to any one specific brand of wax per se- He was just in the market for a quality wax to do its intended job well.. last for a hot minute- especially, if he’s taking the time/energy to hand wax the car and be worth $ spent to do so! Well, this is the trifecta as this covered all the bases!!
In fact, if you look at 3rd photo.. (taken in my dark garage after midnite!) how gorgeous is that?! Its just like a mirror, if it didn’t have bend in the car.. it would show a total image reflection.. I can’t believe this is all on the dang front fender of my car!!

Of course, Murphy’s law went into effect.. ok, that or possibly, it’s just a winter day in utah in Feb.?!! But, about 3hr. post waxing car… we had precipitation- really??! The marks from water drops were a bit visible yet, wiped off/away with the ease of a soft cloth and that was it! The all over snowflakes that landed on the newly waxed target just dissipated- leaving zero trace of water/wet anywhere on the newly waxed job... what!! This morning, as I gaze at my reflection- it still looks fantastic and only thing visible at all, is dust in the air that landed on car.

Armor all brand he tells me gives a high gloss shine only, by day 2... it is already clouding and fading. This has such better staying power- he did some research and swears its due to the ceramic.. so, this is key when looking at what to order!!
Using the Turtle wax spray.. he said to be sure to only use- no more then, 2 pumps of product on each panel of car- even though it May not feel like enough, it’s more then plenty!! As the rag becomes saturated... maybe use a bit less product. Always trying to avoid getting onto car windows... and to polish around window area and just get product on the window casing.. the trick is- just spray a bit of product onto rag (Not in car!) and then, wipe car.. it will keep from a mess/oops getting on your window!! As for longevity of results- I’m now, at day 3, looking shiny as ever still.. this is a must use for any car waxing day! (a key factor into how long it lasts.. is the notice of any cloudiness!? So far, we have had none..!! I’ll update if drastic change or, hard to remove at wash time?!)
If this info helped you.. please, feel free let me know!

Update: so far still killing it!! I just had to inform you all… I am almost a week post wax in the car and the hype is real!! The only left over signs of anything- or just particle dust left from the air. Probably shows us what we don’t want to know we’re inhaling daily.. yikes! But, hey.. car looks fab!

OK, my husband wanted me to add on to my review… He used ceramic wax to polish his bike- and u la la..!!! However he wanted me to take time to mention, he actually used on the chrome as well as the paint. Looking at the photo above, you can see what an incredible shine.. this stuff rocks!

I hope this info helped.. feel free to let me know!

title: Small size capacity for tools- not mom car clutter!!
text:
Love how this mounts to the car- it is great!! The Velcro on the back is a total perk that attaches to the back seat.. love the 3 head rest hooks that go over the seat.. no gapping in the middle and this keeps the integrity of the unit in place. The stitching seems to be strong overall- But, the nets on the bottom level look a bit weak and may be an issue if you filled to capacity. The other issue I had a problem with, is the flaps on the pockets and lining up the Velcro closures.. they aren’t the easiest to close up.
However, biggest reason why I didn’t give the highest stars.. is mainly for capacity and this is where the product lacks!! Having 6-8 pockets that span the entire length of the backseat... you’d think this would be able to hold a lot- but, its NOT the case. The biggest disappointment, I wanted it too so much..
I was looking for a trunk organizer to help a carpool mom... this was just not it! I have kids cleats/balls/windbreaker/water bottles/first aid kit/blanket/umbrella... all the regular things needed to be in the “mom” trunk. The problem is- these pockets were not big enough to fit any of the items I listed- the actual depth of the top row of pockets is about 1”.... and they don’t have a lot/any forgiveness. The bottom is the net material and so, bigger but- can’t get measurement! I hate the soccer ball rolling all over as I drive- I was hoping this could fit inside the net- nope!! So, if that gives you an idea on size of the largest pocket.
Now, if this was listed as a trunk organizer for specifics- such as tools? Or, any smaller size items in a car- it would be a much better fit. But, the broad idea of trunk organizer... lets face it. Most of us have things bigger then the pocket sizes.. and by pockets- think back jean pocket just square shape, not even big enough pocket to fit pair of shoes.. or a ball? Or, picnic blanket... doesn’t work for “trunk” organizer.

title: Love the convenience
text:
This actually came at a great time. Our Hyundai Santa Fe threw a error code on Monday and we were trying to get the car in to have it looked out. This arrived on Wednesday and within 5 minutes we had the code. Turned out it was a Lean Motor Zone 1 error. 10 minutes of googling and we narrowed it down to the fact that we had put E85 in the tank which trips the oxygen sensor. Time and expense of taking the car in avoided... Just need to top it off with full gas for a while until it burns out.

That might be about the perfect example of why everyone should have one of these. Once the domain of shops, now we have the ability to check codes ourselves. At least for the Santa Fe, the code reader port is very accessible, right next to the steering wheel in the fuse box panel. The tool hooks up in seconds and reads the error seconds later. The UI is easy to figure out (didn't use the manual for anything.) The construction is good and fits into the glove box. Love it.

title: Proved to be an interesting and functional idea
text:
I live in Minnesota and have to park outdoors. I am well versed in scraping and would like to do less of it. I'm impressed with this cover. It is simple and fairly easy to install, especially with two people. But perhaps not easy enough to put on without a good reason, like an impending storm.

We go it yesterday and immediately put it on the car to test it and possibly prevent frost and some forecast light snow. First off, there are absolutely no instructions with this product. Even a quick diagram showing how to put it on would be nice. But it is not rocket science, so once we realized that we would be closing the back into the car doors and the front was pulled taut with the hooked elastic straps it was easy. Not -20 degrees in howling wind easy, but easy enough on a calm and not overly cold night.

The product is a thin nylon, think tent material, or a camping tent fly. It is thin and pliable. So it is nearly weightless and needs to be secured to have any chance of not being blown off. It comes neatly folded and slid into its container. But come 6:30 AM in the cold, it is not going to be folded up as carefully and is hard to fit back into the bag. It would be better if it came in some sort of stuff sack, as there will be some stuffing to get it back in.

But despite the lack of instructions and a less than well thought out storage bag, this is a very nice idea. I didn't help much this morning, but I will put it on for future impending storms. I hate scraping.

title: Okay for vehicle tires once you figure it out. Terrible for bicycle tires.
text:
Now that I've gotten used to operating this, it's okay for inflating vehicle tires - and only vehicle tires. In order to program the desired pressure, the device works best when the pressure gauge is popped into the device and power is drawn from the vehicle or an outlet. I've found that the gauge is not sufficiently charged for programming steps unless plugged in. It's nice that it stores the desired psi, starts up again at the next tire, and shuts off when the desired pressure level is reached. If this style of pump meets your needs, I suggest choosing the option that comes with the wall plug.

This is terrible for bicycle tires. I set the desired psi, connect the compressor to the tire by screwing, and inflate. All is fine until I try to remove the pump's tube from the tire. Without quick release, the disconnection process releases entirely too much air. I'm afraid I'll pop my tires if I intentionally over-inflate to account for what will be lost when I disconnect. My bike tires lost at least 6 psi when I disconnected.

I have not yet tried to inflate sports balls with this. I plan to use my new bicycle tire pump for that task. I would not choose this air compressor again.

title: A Darkness in the Light
text:
I have had a run of bad luck with halogen bulbs in my vehicle, and I looked to these bulbs as replacements to end that streak. Unfortunately, these didn’t work for me, at all.

I will start by saying that I was very careful to ensure that these were the right match for my vehicle. My car takes an H11 bulb for the headlights, and I verified that that’s exactly what I was getting. Amazon’s “confirmed fit” tool stated that these were correct. When I received them I verified that, yes, these are indeed the right ones. So far, so good.

Installation was straightforward. Though I am well practiced at replacing the headlight bulbs now, I still read the directions included to make sure I was installing them correctly. They popped in easily and they connected to the electrical system without any trouble at all. Connection was properly snug and the plug snapped into place exactly like it is supposed to.

I turned on the headlights and...nothing. Engine on or off, these simply will not power on. The vehicle doesn’t complain, and everything else works, there’s just no power to the headlamps. I did replace the battery in said vehicle less than 6 months ago so I know that’s not the issue.

The documentation states that if they don’t come on, contact support for a decoder of some kind. If someone is replacing bulbs it’s likely in response to a burned out bulb, not as a preemptive measure, so not including a necessary decoder is akin to not including custom batteries in an electronic device that takes a non-standard battery size.

I’m at a complete loss here. With the bulbs installed properly I should have seen some indicator that they were plugged in, even if it was an error code or something. Instead, I got absolutely nothing. Fortunately these uninstall just as easily and I went back to the current set of halogen bulbs which powered on immediately, so I know I didn’t blow a fuse. Based on my experience with these (which I hope is atypical), I cannot recommend them.

title: I Like These Better Than Foam Plugs
text:
I like going to shows and concerts (though I do not go as often as I would like) and I learned very quickly that ear protection is crucial. When your sinuses actually vibrate inside your head so that it feels like your nose is running, you know it’s loud... Some time back I purchased a large pack of foam ear plugs specifically for attending concerts, and these work great but they’re single use. I was interested in trying these plugs to see how they compare. These compare reasonably well and in the long run are a better value.

These are silicone inserts that are very similar in shape and feel to the silicone tips on in-ear wireless ear buds. They slip in via a little pressure and they stay in because of the bell shape. These have a small filter in each (you can see the filter) that enables some noise in while reducing other noise. It’s a simple and straightforward solution.

One concern I had was, how to get them out once they’re in my ears? The manufacturer thought to put a tab on them that makes it easy to simply pull them out. Even though they create a seal when installed properly, they pop right out without much effort at all.

These are comfortable, relatively speaking. I generally do not like anything in my ears, but ear protection is really necessary at concert venues unless you want to have hearing loss. Foam plugs make my ears itch after a little while, but so far these plugs have not caused me that discomfort. After a few minutes, I no longer even notice them in my ears.

In use they seem to work well. For me, I go to EDM shows which means bass that is turned up way too much and is enough to kill your hearing quickly with no protection. These provide enough protection to filter out sufficient noise to make listening bearable without completely destroying the sound.

As I test, I popped these into my ears and made sure they sealed properly. Then, I put on a good set of headphones, loaded up a track filled with deep bass and screaming highs - basically, a heavy metal instrumental that was heavy on guitars. With this particular set of headphones at the volume I set (maxed out), I usually hit the pain threshold. With these plugs in, the music was muted to a comfortable level, the highs taking the biggest hit but the bass also being toned down a lot. I switched to a very fast, loud, bassy EDM track and the result was the same - subdued music but still clear enough to be enjoyable. The same held true with a guitar-heavy shoegaze track.

These clean up easy, too. Once you use them, give them a quick swab with clean water and if you’re sharing them (not recommended), a little vinegar to disinfect them. The small instruction manual that comes with these says to remove the filter if washing in soapy water.

These are good ear plugs that seem to work as advertised. They’re more comfortable than foam plugs, they are reusable and they reduce loud sounds to comfortable levels.

title: Simple and Straightforward Operation
text:
I will readily admit that I do not need a riveting tool often. Riveting is one of those tasks that I need to do only very occasionally, and I have always done it the “hard way” as I was taught. This was my first time using an actual riveting tool and it is definitely easier than doing everything manually.

Most who would be reading this and looking at this tool already know the basic process and how it works, so I will not bother explaining the full procedure for using such. I will say it works in a way vaguely similar to how anchor screws work.

Included in the package are drill bits, three different sizes of rivets and the rivet tool itself. To say it contains everything you need would be false; at a minimum you need a drill if you do not already have the right sized hole for the rivet you need to place.

The handle has a little side-to-side play in it and it can pinch if you’re not careful. Otherwise, this is a solid tool and it feels like it will last for a long time under moderate use. Because of the wobble in the handle I would probably choose a different tool for more professional work, but it will work on the job if necessary.

As another reviewer noted, there is a mismatch between the product description and the actual contents when it comes to the rivet count. This is an editing error, not a product error, but it is misleading.

As far as the job it does riveting, it works well. It does require a little hand strength but it doesn’t require a death grip either, and operation is simple – squeeze the handle repeatedly until the rivet is firmly in place and the post separates. That’s it – not rocket science.

This tool makes riveting much easier than trying to rivet something completely manually. Until now I didn’t have a good solution for riveting beyond the most basic method I was taught, but now I have an easy solution that works well. The tool cost is reasonable, and it works well enough for almost any home projects.

title: Fine Set of Hammers and Dollies for Metal Working
text:
I have a couple of other tools by YIYITOOLS and these have been quality tools that exceeded my expectations. This set of tools has proven to be of good quality as well and so far I am pleased with it.

This is a tool set that is marketed as geared for auto body repair and maintenance. Having seen someone pound out and repair a car that needed body work several years ago I see how this works and why this set is marketed for that specific use case. These tools are suited for reshaping bent and damaged metal, pounding out creases and reshaping indentations. Using these for those purposes does require some practice, though.

There are three hammers and four dollies in this set. The hammers are specialty hammers that are designed for pounding and shaping, though they will work as regular tack hammers in a pinch. Two of the three have a pointed head on one side, well-designed for tapping. The dollies are also metal shaping tools designed for pounding, and the different shapes make finding the right one that fits into a cramped space easier.

I like the grips on the hammers. They're comfortable and I can maintain my grip even when the hammers get a little wet.

This is not a typical set of hammers and metal blocks. This is a set designed for metal working, and it is designed well for that purpose. It can be used in other contexts, including just for driving nails and so on, but there are better tools for those types of tasks. If you need a set of tools that it designed specifically for working with damaged metal, and you don't want to spend a fortune on it, this is a good tool set that should serve you well.

title: Works Well with House Security System

title: Decent Small Oil Can
text:
My father had an oil can similar to this one in his workshop years ago, and I remember using it when I was younger to get oil to hard-to-reach places that otherwise would be messy when using a simple dropper or an aerosol spray applicator can. I was pleased to have the opportunity to work with this one. So far it has worked well, though there are a couple of fit-and-finish things that could have been done a little better.

This oil can is on the smaller side, holding just a little more than 3/4 cup of oil. This is good for smaller jobs and for cramped areas where a larger applicator might not fit very well. If you need a larger can there are other sizes available. For my needs, this is just about right. The smaller size means lighter weight, which is a plus.

It comes with two applicator nozzles, one straight and rigid and the other bendable. At first I thought the bendable one was just a bendy rubber tube, but when it is bent it holds it shape somewhat, and if very gently squeezed I can feel it has a core of some kind that gives it some structural integrity. The straight nozzle is good for most uses and is the one I will use most often, while the bendy one is for really hard to reach places that the straight nozzle would not touch.

Pressure coming out of the nozzles seems to be decent and I have had no trouble with getting oil from it. The trigger is not adjustable, so the pressure is one-size-fits-all. This is a minor complaint, in that it would be nice to tweak the pressure depending on what you’re doing. When the can is dry, it is difficult to feel anything from the nozzles when you squeeze the trigger but the intake inside the can does draw enough air that you can feel it. Obviously it works better with oil though right out of the box it is tough to know if it works at all before you fill it.

The can is painted bright yellow which is nice for visibility. What is interesting is that the can actually has paint on the inside as well. As long at the paint doesn’t get into the oil this isn’t really an issue, but if it flakes off at all it could be a big deal as it could clog the nozzles.

This is a decent little oil can that will see some use on my house. It seems to work well and I like the color of the can. It could be finished a little better, and a basic pressure adjustment (like a garden sprayer) would be nice, but in the price range that might be asking a bit much. Overall, I am satisfied with it.

title: Much Better than the Cheaper, Slider Types of Gauges
text:
Every other tire gauge I have ever used has a straight bar type with a sliding measure that blows out the bottom to show the pressure. This gauge by TireTek is a lot different and brings more features to the table than those simpler gauges.

First things first - this gauge is much, much larger than any other I have used with the sole exception of one built into an air compressor. The entire (no pun intended) assembly is over a foot long and it has a huge dial gauge on the end. The dial is encased in rubber and this serves two purposes - it protects the dial and it makes the dial assembly look a bit more like a tire.

The dial is very easy to read and it gives a clear reading accurate to within 1 PSI. The range goes from 0 PSI up to 60 PSI in graduations of one. There’s no rocket science here.

Where this gauge adds more is in the pressure release button which you press and hold to slowly release some air from the tire. As you hold it down and the air escapes, the pressure dial slowly drops to show the current pressure so you can stop at any point you like.

I like that fact that even though the joint near the dial is somewhat loose and the unit can be turned about it does not leak air.

This is a well-made gauge. The hose and casing are heavy rubber and will resist most simple cuts and scuffs, and when it is stored properly the rubber should not degrade. The dial is heavy and though it has a plastic face it is solid and can survive a decent drop. The joints between the hose and the metal connector fittings do not leak which is good for maintaining accuracy.

This is a great tire gauge. It’s a solid unit, easy to use and easy to read. It works a lot better than the slider types, too.

title: Lightweight and Inexpensive
text:
Polarized sunglasses are very useful for cutting down reflected light. I use them when I go fishing to cut down on the glare coming off the surface of the water on sunny days. I have used multiple pairs of polarized sunglasses and this pair is a good one, particularly when considering how inexpensive they are.

This is a very lightweight pair of glasses and they feel like they weigh nothing when they are being worn. They are half-frames so they cut down on the amount of material and add some style to them at the same time. They are mostly black with yellow trim. They came in a semi-hard crush-resistant case which is a nice touch.

One of the main concerned I had was build quality. I have used other sets of inexpensive sunglasses and they have been flimsy or have broken outright after a short time. These seem to be better made than that. They have a little flexibility to them and the hinges and nose piece are attached with tight screws. There is no play in the hinges. And, the lenses are attached correctly and do no jiggle at the corners like I have seen with other half-frame solutions.

The polarization is excellent and is aligned properly (which can be tested against an LCD computer screen). When they are held level they provide light reduction as expected. As they are rotated polarized light fades until it is almost completely dark at 90 degrees.

Overall these are nice sunglasses and they seem to be made very well. The price on these is very low too and that makes them a good deal.

title: Weatherproof Flashing Marker - Lots of Uses!
text:
Lights and reflectors are a good method of attracting attention, either to alert of the need for caution or to draw specific attention to a specific place like a driveway. Solid reflectors are common in rural areas and are used to mark road entrances. This solar flasher is an excellent way to draw attention to drivers and people on foot as well. Having spent time living on a farm I can see numerous possibilities.

This is a cylindrical light, 2.75" in diameter and about 3" tall (just counting the reflective red light enclosure) and is capped by a solar panel. It collects light during the day and when the light level gets sufficiently low it beings to flash. The flash is very bright but is not blinding and it can be seen clearly at a distance.

The base of the light has a pressure clamp that is tightened by a single screw. It can accommodate a pole approximately 2" in diameter, less if using a padding material like rubber insulation. So, this will work for some fence posts - if you intent to mark a fence, measure the pole diameter to ensure this light will clamp properly or plan to add an extra pole to account for it.

The light’s switch is located under the base and is a small, black slider. This is smart placement as it is hard to mess with once the light has been affixed in place. It does mean that if you want to turn off the light it must be unmounted from wherever it has been placed.

This light is completely sealed and is waterproof so it can be left outside regardless of the weather.

One thing I am not sure of yet is the effective run time. I have not tried to run it all night but it does run for a good while from what I have determined in testing. I also have not yet determined the full charge time when it has been run down. So far it has shown no signs of weakening.

I can see numerous uses: marking the entrance to a road or driveway, alerting to the edge of water, marking a structure on a body of water like a boat house or buoy, indicating the corner of a fence, marking a dangerous structure like a parked piece of heavy equipment, and when used with multiple units can mark a trail. This fall, it will be used to mark our flag as we navigate a cornfield maze at one of the local farms. There are many other ideas for this light; this is just a few possibilities.

This is a fine flashing light that works well and requires zero maintenance. It gathers solar energy so it does not require a power source, it flashes very brightly when operating and it is sealed to keep moisture out. Overall, I am pleased with it.

title: Cleans Deep Stains and Dirt
text:
In the past I had never used a cleaning solution just for leather, relying mainly on a heavy cloth and warm, soapy water. Wild Bill's Leather Cleaner was my introduction to a dedicated leather cleaner, and I was curious just how well it worked so I gave it two very solid tests - a pair of leather dress shoes I have had for about 20 years and a pair of heavy leather work gloves that have been used for everything from electrical work to hauling tree branches.

To be fair, the leather shoes may be old but they are in relatively good shape, just in need of cleaning. The gloves, however, are atrocious and are stained with worn-in dirt.

The leather cleaning solution is a cloudy white solution that actually has a pleasant smell, somewhat like lemon-scented dish detergent. This was a very pleasant surprise - I expected a harsh chemical smell. As a bonus, the fragrance is not strong so it does not require use in a ventilated area. I added a little to a clean, soft cloth and set to work on the shoes. The shoes are not brand new and considering their age I did not expect miracles; that said, the leather cleaner did a great job of removing surface dirt and dust and made the shoes look years younger than they really are - far better than my damp cloth with soapy water ever could.

The miracle was in how well the cleaner worked on the leather heavy work gloves. Originally a warm shade of tan, the palm of my gloves have been dirtied to an ugly gray (and the fingers are even worse). I applied the cleaner to the cloth again and rubbed in a circular motion in the middle of the palm. It took some work but most of the dirt lifted as I scrubbed. It's not perfectly clean but the palm of my glove looks a lot better than it did!

Wild Bill's leather cleaner does an excellent job of cleaning and rejuvenating leather surfaces. I used it on a particularly soiled article and it cleaned that surface better than I could have asked. This is an excellent product.
