title: no show socklettes
text: I purchased 2 different types and these are my favs of the two.  they come up way higher on the top of my feet, which works for the shoes I wear and the fit.  I have a size 7 foot and an 8 1/2 (womens) foot due to a deformity.  There are 3 little zig zag silicone strips that help to keep the sock in place on your heel.  I purchased the black and they are a dark black.  The sock is fairly thin, but not see through.  The socks are very stretchy.  I find them comfortable.  I probably will buy more of these.  Oh, and as for washing, I have a delicate bag and I wash them in the bag and then lay them flat to dry in my dryer closet.  Having said all of that, I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: no see socklettes
text: These work well... but I have to report that if you have a size 7 1/2 or smaller foot, these will easily slip off.  Due to having had polio when I was a child, I have one foot that is a size 7 and the other that is an 8 1/2.  So I am uniquely able to discuss this discovery.  They fit perfectly on my 8 1/2 foot... but with my smaller foot, I just can't keep the sock on.  There is a silicone heel back - which will help if the sock fits your foot.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: wacoal bra
text:
Ok..I made a mistake. This bra is NOT thinly foam lined. It's just 2 pieces of nylon. I wear a 38DDD. This is a front loader - so there are not back hook adjustments. It cuts pretty hard - so I would NOT consider this bra "all day comfort" as the tag says. On the upside, the underwire is lifting. But, the cup was not enough for my bust. I went back and ordered the 40DDD to see if that helps with cup and comfort. The do offer a 38G - but I worry about the tightness. Listen, you do want a pretty snug fit - because the elastic will stretch. And in this case there are no tighter hooks to go to. But it was so uncomfortable I didn't think I could take the wait to a stretched out band. The straps are about 3/4" wide and are adjustable. I do wish there was a thin foam lining. Wacoal is a good brand and it appears well made. There is a slight decor of stretch lace at the cleavage V - so it gives a bit of feminine edge. The lace lays flat and I didn't notice it under my T shirt. The back strap is NOT terrible wide. So if you're afraid of "back fat" this might not be the bra for you. It hit ok under the arm for me but I can see that some may have issues with fat there too. All in all it's not my least favorite but I can't wear my size. U really like a front loader, but it is SUPER hard to find one built for my bust size I guess. Even harder doing it all online. I will check in after I get the 38G to compare the fit and update my review with that info in case if might be helpful.
UPDATE... The 38G rib cage fit was a slightly more comfortable feel and the cups were deeper... but... the way the underwire is sewn it pushes down on your cleavage creating a very big cleavage bulge.. Eh. While I really tried to make this style work, it doesn't for me. I am returning both. I would say that if you are DDD or larger, I would pass on this style. Having said that.. Wacoal is a very good brand and well made. I would try some other styles. I plan to.

title: vanity fair bra
text:
I purchased the 38DD - REALLY needed the DDD or E/F (which is not offered). There really isn't any "separation" and I did miss the part where it didn't have an underwire.
PROS: I like the neutral color. The straps were wide at the right spots - IF you criss/cross them. A nice wide back strap, four hooks. It looks very well made.
CONS: The material snags really easily. If you don't criss cross the straps - the wide part of the strap is too far down your chest - thus cutting into your shoulder (I get that I don't have small boobs - but this hurts after a while). No underwire for better lift. While it looks well made, it is VERY --- not feminine. Looks like a battle bra - which I was willing to go with if it would have just given me the right fit.
Most of my stars are construction. One star for snaggy material and straps that aren't wide where they need to be. This LOOKS like a bra meant for women with larger busts - but honestly, it's not really made very well for that - in my opinion.

title: rubber bottomed socks

title: boys shoes
text: The shoes ran true to size in my opinion.  HOWEVER... the ad is SO deceptive.  They show the last three letters of the "brand"  as IKE.... Now.  What do you THINK you're buying? I have had other fleece robes in the past that were very bulky - less desirable.  I wanted a warm, cozy robe but without some of the bulk.  And these robes fit the bill.  They washed and dried beautifully.  They do run a tiny bit large. So it depends on how you like your robes to fit - super loose? I would stick to my regular size.  A little less loose?  Maybe go down a size.  I did go down and they are plenty roomy.  The shorter wrap around robe is a bit shorter than I would have liked - hits me above my knee (I am 5'7") but still workable.  I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seem useful.

title: Amazon suitcase
text:
UPDATE BELOW.....Wow. These suitcases are AWESOME for the price! I was expecting a lot less. I purchased 3. I chose the bright, safety orange. Easy to see in the sea of other colors for sure. The outer shell is hard - sturdy feeling. The inside is roomy. They are around 5-6" deep in each side (I've included some pics - sorry about holding the ruler upside down - but you can see it's about 5 to 6") One side is zipper closed, the other side has elastic straps to contain contents. The outer zippers are sturdy feeling and run smoothly. There is also an 'extender' zipper giving you an extra 2" or so in depth. Honestly, these suitcases 'feel' as nice as some others I have purchased for literally 4x the price! All the nice care points too with the inner zipper, and additional pockets. It looks and feels like a suitcase way beyond the price point. Now, in all fairness, they are new to me and I will be using them on a trip in about a week. So, I will update my review should new info seem useful. The ad says they weigh just under 10lbs.. I used my handheld suitcase scale and it registered 9.1 lbs empty. One of the pics I included shows me holding a 12" ruler so you can get an idea of the width of the inside of the cases. The pull out handle is not as 'sturdy' feeling as I would like... but it works- It locks down and lifts easily. It appears or feels like the pullout handle is plastic at the handle part.. the bar appears to be lightweight aluminum - so it might be bent with lots of use.. we'll see. There are two grab handles one on the top and one the side of case. The outer wheels are multi-directional... and stick out quite a bit and I'm not sure they are as 'sturdy' as the rest of the case. If there is an 'Achilles heel' on these bags... the wheels may be it or possibly the pull handle.. but we as I said, time will tell and I never hesitate to update. I've included some pics and hope my review was helpful to you.
UPDATE: 12/4/2019.... Have taken these suitcases through the airline system two times so far... NO problems to report. I am happier and happier with this purchase... but time will tell and I update if new info seem useful.

title: new vanity fair front close bra
text:
UPDATE BELOW 6/26/2018....
If you HAVE been using the Vanity Fair front closing - 75339, BUT you have been WISHING for more coverage - THIS version is slightly better. I've been wearing the other version for many, many years. I keep asking for and WISHING for a 38DDD - but to no avail so I buy the 38DD. Why? Because I find it comfortable and NOT over padded. I like a thin lining for comfort, but don't desire additional "size" with the filling. This version gives you ALMOST 1 more inch in the cup at the small size... at least on the 38DD. If you wore the 38DD in the "lighter" version, I would recommend buying the same size of this "fuller" version. I still really need a 38DDD, but I can definitely make this work. This version IS convertible to a racer back, just like the older version - although I rarely use that option, it's nice to have. Other improvements include - slightly wider - different material straps. FAR less "cutting" into the top of your shoulder - further - the back strap is slightly wider.. The front closure is still plastic - but I have yet to have one "fail." The down side of front closure bra is that as you wear it, as with ALL bras, the elastic "gives" and with the front closure, there are no adjustments. Still I get a fair amount of wear out each one - more than a year. For the price, I think this good. Camel Camel these so that you can grab them when they are an even better price - which has always beat what they are offered to me locally. There is a thin fiber fill - but it doesn't add bulk - just modesty. And the cup is smooth - there is some strategically placed lace that doesn't create lumps and bumps on the bra - a pretty touch. The other think I notice is that this newer version "feels" more supportive. I think there is a visible lift - meaning more support. The straps are adjustable, and as I said above, much more comfortable that the older, smaller version. Bras are SUPER personal and every one of us is different, but I was hoping to share enough details and comparisons to be helpful. I never hesitate to update my reviews should new info seems useful. Honestly, I think this bra is worthy of shot if you liked the older version but were wishing for a bit more cup.
UPDATE 6/26/2018..... I just wanted to say that I ordered the 40DD. As I have mentioned above, I'd prefer a 38DDD or even an E... but that isn't offered in this style... so I decided to "try" the 40DD. I had feared it would be too big around, but it is actually fine... SLIGHTLY larger, but not significantly around... the "UP" part is that you get at LEAST 1/2" more in cup coverage. To me, that's worth while. Every woman is built uniquely and bras are SO hard, especially mail order. If you prefer a front loader... are full size.. and prefer an underwire for support, these are worth a try. I recommend possibly trying one size around "up" if you'd like a bit more cup.
I have had no issues with poor performance in wear or otherwise, however, I DO wash in a lingerie bags, on delicate and hang them to dry in my dryer "closet." Hope this helps you in some way!

title: Knit mink
text:
Sadly, this jacket was ruined by the terribly sewn inner lining, especially around the tag. It's so awful It would be hard to sell at an super cut outlet. Further the seller appears to have known this when they sent it out stating that it didn't seem to effect the wear. Seriously? Not for this price. I have included pics for you to see. I did return the jacket immediately. I do feel compelled however to share my thoughts about the jacket
1. The fur appears to be mink. It is not very soft.. but that is because the mink has not been sheared, so the stiffer, longer hairs are still present. I own several very high quality minks and I usually choose the sheared pelts as they are so much softer. The color is good. Fairly deep and rich looking. The pic I included was with full sun on it to show the pelts and the knit better.
2. This jacket is "knitted" using remnants of mink pelts. The "knitting" means there is a slight "give" or stretch to the jacket. The sizing to me appears to be spot on. I did go one size larger in order to accommodate sweaters underneath. I had considered traveling with this jacket.
3. The inner lining is a very, very cheap crepe. After consulting with my furrier*, the quality of the crepe was so inferior in order to "repair" the lining sewing it would necessary to completely remove the lining and start over. Far more cost than the value of the jacket. He also advised me that the low quality of the lining material is such that it will tear and not bear up to regular wear. *Furrier is my storage, care and alteration specialist - NOT a fur salesmen.
4. The sleeves are extraordinarily long. I actually liked this, however, you should know you cannot fold the sleeve over as to the lining and sewing construction of the jacket. So the sleeves fell almost down to my finger tips. You can kind of see this on the model wearing the jacket.
5. The "crush" collar does in fact create a floppy hood of sorts, but is sticks out in odd angles because of the "shoulder" humps that keep the collar down around your shoulders when it is not a hood.
6. The jacket has fur hooks for closures down the front and at the neck if you decide to pull the hood up and use as a hood.
7. It claims to be, and SORT of is, a semi swing coat... meaning wider at the bottom than at the chest... sort of A shaped... HOWEVER.. the hem is so horribly sewn that it is terribly uneven all around. In fact, the hem looks as though it is longer at both hips and then shorter in the front and back. One side being longer than other. Further, it was quite long. Falling well below my knees and I'm 5'7".
Over all, it was just horrible construction. Dealing with this seller has been challenging as well. I will not be a return customer. Amazon had to step in to help facilitate the return. Shouldn't have been necessary as it was a straight up, immediate return.

title: Leather jewelry box
text:
UPDATED REVIEW BELOW
The jewelry box = about 4 stars
The musty, moldy STINK that permeates this entire box inside and out.... negative 5 stars... So 2 stars is very generous.

I noticed that having the side flaps open helped the top lid stay open.
Here is the bottom line... when I opened the box an OVERWHELMING musty, moldy odor nearly knocked me over. I don't consider myself to be overly sensitive to odors, however, this odor lingered in my living room for days. Now, this is supposed to be "leather." It does have a very, very faint smell of leather... but it is easily overtaken by the must and mold. :( I am attempting several strategies to remove the smell... but if you put anything in it, it is going to envelop that awful odor. First I opened it all up, removing drawers and dividers and let it set in the sun for an entire day. For the last 2 days I have been spraying it with a Febreeze like antibacterial spray 3 times a day. I don't really think I am making headway.
It is likely going to the closest donation center... OR... perhaps my husbands tool shop. Pretty fancy for nuts and bolts, but who cares if they stink? I always update my reviews if new info would be useful. In this case and at this time, I just cannot recommend it for purchase.
UPDATE: 11/13/2016.... Ultimately I was not able to remove the overwhelming odor emitted by the box. I felt it was so bad that I couldn't really take it to a donation center either. The bag itself isn't terribly heavy which is good. When I "load" it with everything I need it's still reasonably weighted... 3-5 lbs (?) It came with a storage/dust bag, a nice touch, although it will probably not spend much time in it. It arrived quickly (I have prime) along with some other things I had ordered. title: Love these
text:
I ordered two. Shipping is a little slow, but they arrived in good condition. First, these bags are huge. I weighed them with my luggage hook and it said 9 pounds, just as advertised. Lots of neat features. The wheels are protected by little edges and reinforced corners, so they may last a bit longer when battered by the baggage handlers. There is a extender zip, but honestly they are so huge inside I can't imagine using it. As I was unpacking them I discovered there is a handle on the bottom where the wheels are! What a brilliant idea. This means you can grab this suitcase just about any way it lands. SUPER handy when you're chasing your bag around the carousel because it landed wheel side toward you. There was a bit of chemical smell when I opened them, but I just aired them out and it is greatly reduced. I might lightly mist them with some Febreeze. But only if the smell lingers. The zippers are very heavy duty and the main zips do have the lock loop. Inside there is a flat, top zip area and two adjustable straps on the bottom main compartment with a small side, mesh zip bag that is attached. Pretty standard confirguration inside. There is a limited warranty for manufacturer defect only and NO airline or consumer abuse and/or normal wear issues.
I did purchase the basic black because they were cheaper, but here's a tip: I use permanent sharpie pens (gold, silver and copper - sold on Amazon for about $5.99 a set of three) and a stencil (also on Amazon and themes to fit everyone out there... at about $7.00 a sheet) to personalize my suitcases so they are quick and easy to spot on the baggage carousel.. even at a distance. Because they are uniquely decorated, no one ever confuses my bag for theirs. Win/Win.
Tag inside one bag said "Designed in the USA, made in China" Thought about docking one star for that part....
I travel a lot and will update if there are any wear or other issues.
UPDATE 6/15/2014: The chemical smell is a bit more than I'd like... doing the Febreeze and I think a day out in the sun. Some might consider a "new car" type smell, however, I am sensitive to chemical smells in general.

title: Know before you buy
text:
BEFORE BUYING you should know:

1. They are in Thailand. If you have to return the item for any reason, it will cost YOU approximately $20. (Mine was $18.95 from Oregon) They (Koh Koh) will also ask you to declare the value of the return as $10.00 so they do not get charged tax for the item being returned. No where in the Amazon posting does it indicate these dresses are shipping from (and returned to) Thailand. It does says "FREE SHIPPING WORLDWIDE"... but that doesn't tell you anything really. I will say that it arrived relatively quickly. Too bad it was the dress was such a terrible mess. ** UPDATE** 9/25 After a long communication "battle" a full refund, including my shipping has been processed.

2. I actually really like the design of this dress. However, when the dress arrived (I ordered the red and white), the red part of the print had bled into the white and in some areas there were big red sploches on the white area of the graphic print. The bleed so bad that what should have been crisp, clean lines of the graphic design where "blurred" over the entire dress. I can't believe they actually shipped it to me in this condition. I would have liked to have ordered other colors (the navy/white and the black/white), but I will not risk they will be color bled or worse. What if it is a cleaning issue? Possibly a bad dye batch? Who knows? The dress I received should never have been sent out.

DRESS DESIGN INFO: I will say that I found the sizing to be acurate per their provided info. The material hangs well and SHOULD be machine wash/tumble or hang dry, although I am not able to atest to that as it was immediately returned. The dress material is very thin but not see thru. To be honest, since it was such a hot mess I did not really inspect the sewing quality. The dress (design and material hand) does not look like a million dollar dress, but it would work nicely for casual wear or casual evening wear in my opinion. I also believe the design of the dress is one that would be flattering on a wide range of women and it is nice they offer some larger sizes. The red is sort of a brick and the photo is fairly accurate as to the color, and the white was a little more ivory/pink, but that is probably due to the ink bleed of the red onto the white. I did not find the "V" neck too low for me, but it would be possible to wear a cami under for modesty.

I strive to provide honest and geniunely helpful reviews each time I do so. I hope it has been helpful to provide this info.

I enclosed photos wearing Brooks gts adrenaline 21 gts on the left prosthesis, reebok royal nylon on the right foot, and an Athletic Work (very inexpensive shoe from Walmart) that I wear around the house.

title: Steer clear if you’re tall
text: This sizing on this dress is just nuts. I bought the dark blue and red in size XL. I’m 5’10” and typically in a size 16/18. I was able to physically get the dress on, but that’s it. The buttons ended way too high up, right at crotch level and the arms were very tight. If you’re tall or have a long torso, I don’t see this working for you. The length and overall style was awkward as well, this would only look cute on someone who is petite with a smaller frame

title: Not as good as they used to be
text: So I've purchased 15 pairs of Oalka leggings since early 2018. They used to be amazing, the fabric was thick and had good compression. Not slippery or shiny. These were the style that didn't have pockets. I've seen purchased a few pairs with the pockets over the past year and they're totally different. The material is thinner and more slick, the crotch tends to shimmy down and they just don't feel nearly as good as they used to be. Oalka used to be my holy grail for both workout and everyday wear, but not so much anymore

title: Still great two years later
text: I bought these to use in the hospital after delivery two years ago and they were perfect. Thick and cushy, plenty of grip on the bottom and they come up high on the back of the ankle to prevent rubbing if you wear them with shoes. I’m a size 12 womens and got the XL, they fit great with plenty of room. I still wear them around the house since they prevent slipping on wood floors

title: Total waste of money
text: The size is fine, and that’s the only positive thing I can say about these shorts. The fabric is see through and the stitching on these are so awful. They are supposed to have the paper bag style waist and the stitching is just all over the place along the waistband. I’ve purchased from the Milumia brand before and these are a huge disappointment

title: Ripped already
text: I buy a lot of different, inexpensive leggings and at first these seemed to be pretty average. The fabric is on the thinner side, though comfortable and the sizing was accurate. Today is my second time wearing them though and the thigh just ripped, that's literally never happened to me before. Cheap

title: Needs improvements
text: At first these sleepers fit as expected. I bought two to test out and was immediately impressed and loved the designs, so I ordered two more. Well now that I’ve washed the first set of sleepers two times, I regret buying more because the dark blue has faded a ton and shrunk a good 2-3 inches in the leg. These went from having some extra room to grow into to just fitting perfectly. I compared the washed sleeper to the brand new one so I can confirm that it’s a big difference. Not too pleased, I can get more reliable quality from a $5 sleeper from Walmart.

title: Great dress
text: I’m 5’10”, about 230lbs and a size 16/18 or XL/2X in tops usually with a 40D chest. I got this in a 2x and it fit great, maybe just a smidge too by but I’d say it’s pretty true to size. It’s a beautiful dress, vibrant and flowy. I’m returning it due to how long it is on me. I’m used to dresses fitting me shorter due to my height but this is so long and I just don’t ever wear long or maxi type dresses. I’m going to order the shorter version of these dresses instead.

title: Pleased with the suit
text:
I’m 5’10”, roughly 230lbs and a size 16/18 jeans and usually an XL in tips. I got the swimsuit in a size 16/18 and it fit as expected, I didn’t need to size up at all. The bottoms covered well without being too cheeky and they came up to my belly button, which is something that I want after two kids. They don’t do an amazing job at smoothing or tummy control but they also aren’t advertised to do that at all.

I typically go for black suits because I am self conscious of this but got the white floral top with the teal bottoms and am happy I went out on a limb to stray from the black, it looks just like the picture.

As for the top, I’m a 40D and it’s a bit snug. It fits fine but is a tiny bit tight through the armpits. I don’t think it’s a size issue though, that’s more to do with the fact that I’m carrying some extra quarantine weight right now. I can’t remark on durability or how well the color holds up with use yet since I just got it but if it seems to start fading really quickly or any other issues, I’ll update my review. Overall I’m pretty happy with it, it’s a step up from a boring old mom suit but I still feel pretty secure and covered up in it.

title: Sizing is accurate
text: Bought this for fall so haven’t gotten to actually wear it yet but have washed and tried it on. The sizing is pretty spot on and it washed well, no fading or shrinking. I’m right between an XL and a 2X in tops, depending on the cut and style and got this in a 2X since I wanted it to be looser like picture and it fits well. The sleeves also are long enough, I’m 5’10” and have long limbs and chunky arms and they aren’t tight at all. If they had other patterns I’d consider buying more

title: Avoid, you can buy better quality from Walmart and for cheaper.
text: The sizing of this was fine, accurate for me. Unfortunately that’s about the only thing that’s fine with this product. Like everyone else has said, I also received a nightgown that isn’t sewn up in the front. The area in the bust that is twisted, it’s just left open. The fabric is ok, I’d wash this in a bag (or hand wash) and then hang dry because the straps are very fetching and the fastenings used for adjusting them are super cheap. The big issue here is that there are multiple reviews left about the downfalls of this nightgown, and they aren’t changing it. Typically companies use the feedback to better their products. They also emailed me, asking for feedback. I gave it. Their response was to return it to Amazon. Well that would be great and all but the return window has closed. Their reply was just “ok”. So here is the review you were asking for.

title: Pants that make no sense
text:
I am normally a 16/18 and size XL. I'm pregnant and wanted to find some alternatives to maternity leggings so decided to just size up to a 2X to test them out. I'm still pretty early and haven't changed much in the stomach area and they were close to snug in the waistline, and the legs were oddly baggy in spots. Which never happens with me, I have pretty sturdy legs and never have issues with leggings being baggy on me.

The most ridiculous part of these pants though is that they have these mesh cutouts in strange spots, like a long triangular section right on the hip that starts about mid-top of the thigh and goes clear up to the waistband. So you either need to wear black underwear with it or none at all, because it will absolutely show through.

title: I found it to run a bit small
text:
First off, this isn’t French terry material. It’s normal sweatshirt material. It’s nice, but not French terry, that is a totally different fabric.

Anyway, this does run relatively true to size, but it’s definitely not oversized. I am usually a size XL, sometimes size up to a 2X to have extra room and sleeve length on tops like this but came across a review that said it ran a bit big. Absolutely not, I am returning this because it’s too small. It runs tight through the shoulders and chest for sure. So I would suggest to size up unless you like a semi form fitting hoodie.

title: Fits as expected
text:
I am 5'10" and about a size 16/18, I typically am a size XL, but like to size up the 2X if possible when it comes to items that have long sleeves or where overall length could be an issue, which I chose to do with this dress. I'm glad I did, it fits great. I have pretty long arms and the length on the sleeve is just fine, the skirt hits me right at the knee. The chest fits well too, I am a 40D. The fabric didn't seem overly stretched out or anything. I got this on sale for around $15 I believe and at that price, I am happy with it. I am not sure that I would willingly spend more than about $20-25 max on it though. The black is nice, the fabric is on the thinner side but isn't terrible and it doesn't look "cheap", but I don't know if I would try my luck with any of the prints though.

If you are right between sizes, or are tall, have long arms, bigger chest, etc... then I would consider sizing up if possible. But I think you might also be ok with getting your normal size, just depends on your build really.

title: Runs small
text: This ran a bit small and the fabric was cheap. I got it on sale for around $13-$15 I believe and it was still too much to be worth keeping.

title: Runs a bit small
text: I'm 5'10" and pretty much an XL / size 16 in clothing. This dress came down to right around or at the tops of my knees, so the length was good but the chest was too tight and the fabric was too thin. The fabric stretched too much at the chest and you could see my bra right through it. If it was made out of a nicer, thicker fabric, I probably could have made it work. But will have to return these. I bought it in the dark red and navy, same issue with both. If they offered a 2x, then I would be glad to re-order the next size up but it seems that they only go to xl.

title: Perfect sandals
text: Love them. I never understood why people would pay so much for a pair of sandals before, but now I get it. I have had mine for a couple of months now, they took about a week to break in and are super comfortable. I am now looking to buy a second pair in the more classic two strap design.

title: Does run small.
text: I am a 40D/38C (depending on current weight) so according to the size chart, I ordered a large. Now I know very well that when it comes to bras like this, I am NEVER a large. So I also ordered it in an XL to be safe. Sure enough, the L was too small. I physically could wrestle it on to my body but it was very tight. I do like the bra enough though to keep the XL that I got and am planning on ordering it in the other 2 colors that are available as well.

title: Decent sneakers
text:
So far they seem fine. I'm about an 11.5 in shoes but like to size up to a 12 if possible, which I did here. I'm glad I did size up because they fit perfectly, so I would say that they seem to run about a half size short.

I got these on sale for around $15 I believe. I wouldn't pay much more than $15-20 for them really though. They are good for the price so far.

title: As expected, good for the price.
text: They fit just as expected, wash up well and minimal fading. They are pretty high rise though and I'm 5'10" so I would keep that in mind if you are more on the petite side. I believe I paid around $18 or so at the time and I would pay that again for them.

title: Awful sandals!
text:
These are just awful. First off, the sizing is wrong. About two sizes too small. I am typically an 11-11.5 in shoes but in sandals I go up to a 12, so got these in a 12 and they don’t fit at all. If I had to guess, they may be more like a 10.

Even if they did fit, I still wouldn’t keep them. The quality of these are terrible. If these were like 10 bucks, it would be more understandable. But I paid close to $30 for these and they are just gross. Weird plastic type material is used for the straps, when you try to adjust the straps, the glitter just comes off in chunks and flakes everywhere. You can go to Walmart and spend $12 on better sandals.

title: Way too small
text: I wanted to love this dress but had to return it. I am 5'10" and about a 16, 38C cup.  I can normally do an XL in dresses and due to the reviews that said to order up, I did buy this in a 2X. The bottom half of the dress was fine, great length on me and I liked the fabric. The issue is with the top half of the dress, it most definitely runs very small. I couldn't button it up all the way and the sleeves were extremely tight. Had I tried to bring my arms to my chest, I would have probably ripped out the back of the dress. I don't commonly have issues with sleeves or the chest of tops and dresses running small on me at all, so I know its the sizing of it. Especially since the bottom half was completely fine. If the top wasn't so crazy small, I would have loved this dress.

title: Nice top
text: I'm normally a size XL in tops and ordered this in the same size. Many of the reviews said that it ran big but I didn't find that to be true at all, it fits very well and I think its a cute shirt. The navy isn't quite as dark as the picture depicts it but it's still a dark blue. It fits pretty much just like the picture.

title: great sandals
text: The fit on these are great. I am about an 11.5-12, depending on the type of shoe. I ordered these in a 12 and they are perfect. I do have a bit of room in the back so I could have gone down a half size if they offered it. Super comfortable and I got a 2 pack for a great price, not much more than buying one pair on its own.

title: Don't size up, not necessary
text: I am either a 38C or 40D, depending on my weight. Many of the reviews stated that this runs small so I ordered it in a 40 and its too big. I got it on the tightest hook and it fits there but is almost too loose. So I would suggest to order it in your normal size. So I am returning due to the sizing issue, if I lose anymore weight at all it will be completely useless, also it doesn't serve the purpose I bought it for anyway so I won't re-order in a smaller size.

title: Runs large
text:
Size stats: I am 5'10" and a size 16 (size XL typically in tops and 16 pants). I ordered this in a size large due to many of the reviews stating that the dress runs pretty big and those people are absolutely right. I normally get an XL, sometimes even a 2X in dresses if the sizing is a bit off and a large in this fits me well.

For any tall people out there, this actually works pretty well as a dress, comes down to just a couple of inches above the knee. I even tried belting it and it was still long enough for me to feel comfortable wearing it as a dress. I don't think it is super flattering on my body though but it does seem like it would work pretty good for a nightgown instead, so I will keep it.

title: Great shorts
text: Got these for my daughter in a size small, she is about a juniors 5-7. The quality seems good, a thick fabric. The red color that I got isn't sheer at all. Would buy again when she grows out of them

title: Nice leggings
text: I'm 5'10" and size 16, the XL in these fits really well. I got them in black and they are opaque, don't seem to show anything through at all. My only gripe about them is the crotch on them seems to hang weird on me, like I have to yank it up every so often which I tend to not have to do in other pairs that I have from a couple of different brands. This could just be how they fit on my particular body type. They are still good quality though and I continue to wear them. If I saw them on sale, I wouldn't hesitate to pick up another pair.

title: Nice nightgown, would buy again
text: 5'10" and a size 16 (sometimes 18 if I'm honest) and the XL fits well. Comes down to right above my knees and the fabric feels nice. I would definitely throw this in a lingerie bag and hang to dry if you remember to, I've only recently started doing this and have another similar nightgown (different brand though) that I never did that with and the lace on it is pretty beat up and likes to stick to itself. That isn't anything wrong with the item though, just basic care instructions for your clothes that I'm really just now following.

title: Great sandals
text:
I didn't get to keep these due to them being too small but am still rating them based off of my experience with them. The sizing isn't an issue with the shoes, I'm really more of an 11.5 or even a 12 in some styles but wanted to try my luck with an 11 and they were just a bit too short.

Super comfortable though and I got them for a great price, wish I could keep them.

title: Nice for wide feet
text: I'm actually an 11-11.5 in shoes, sometimes even a 12 in some styles but this size 11 fits me well. The shoes are really comfortable and I got them for a good price, any higher though (I paid around $25) than I don't think they would have been as great of a deal since the heel is made out of some cheapish feeling foam. I have wide feet, I could see where the fit at the toe strap could be an issue for anyone that doesn't have wide feet as well. The sole is nice and squishy.

title: Love them
text:
I love the Oalka brand leggings. I have several pairs now of both the leggings and capri length and I've been impressed enough with the quality to buy about 6 pairs now.

I'm 5'10" and about a 16, I got these in XL and they fit very well. The fabric is nice and sturdy, really smooths you out while staying opaque. I'm pear shaped, so have a big butt and thighs but don't have problems with these sheering out and showing underwear underneath. I have purchased the black and also the space dye camo purple, space dye camo black and space dye charcoal. The solid colors do seem to be a thicker fabric than the prints but the prints are still great. The capri length come down to the same point on my leg as its pictured, so they don't run too short.

title: Great bag, bought it twice
text:
This bag is great, holds a ton of stuff and is sturdy. When you aren’t using it, it zips down into this compact size so it’s super easy to store. I bought one a couple of years ago and have used it multiple times. Was needing a second bag for a trip and came back to buy the exact same one.

Really handy for travel, overnight trips, the gym etc...

Only thing I would suggest is to have more colors, maybe a dark purple, dark green, etc...

title: Perfect after nearly a year
text:
I've now had this ring for almost a year. It has held up well, still shiny and has zero scratches. I wear it every single day and can be rough on my hands. It fits very comfortably. Was coming back to see if it was still available so I could order a smaller size due to losing weight so that should be a testament to how much I like it.

I had purchased a few different rings last year and this is the one I kept due to the nice, pure silver/white color it had. It wasn't yellowy or a darker gunmetal type color at all. Just a bright silver.

title: OK but needs some improvement.
text:
I ordered this in the navy blue, mostly because I really liked the contrast of the white buttons that it has in the photos. Well it came with matching buttons.

For the pros: It does fit well and pretty accurately. I'm 5'10 and a 16/18 in clothing right now, ordered this in an XL. It buttoned up fine and technically it does fit. The fabric is ok. It could stand to be a little thicker, but its not so thin that it will cause issues with sheerness. If needed, you can always just put on a light slip for the bottom.

Cons: I'm not sure how I'm going to make the bust area of this dress work. But it's really cute so I'm going to keep it and try. I'm a 38C and not very large at all. I have a broad chest but not particularly full. The point that I'm getting at is that I don't necessarily have a ton to cover, but there just needs to be a bit more fabric in the cups. Anyway that I tie it, I either get boob coming out the bottom near where it ties or out the top. I just wasn't expecting it to be quite so revealing. I'm going to work with it though and see if I can find a sticky bra that works or something like that. Also, if you aren't naturally pretty perky, its going to be a challenge to find a bra option that will get you sitting high enough for the chest to look flattering. There is no real support in the fabric. I think a big improvement would be to add some type of sewn in cups to the top, that would really help.

title: Fits large
text: I'm a 16/18 and usually am an XL in tops but tend to size up if its long sleeved due to having long arms. I did that with this top and its huge. Super wide and arms are almost too long. I could have gone down 1 or maybe even 2 sizes in this.

title: Great leggings
text:
I came across these as a lightning deal and decided to take a chance while on an ongoing search for good, OPAQUE, black leggings that aren't super thin. These are great. I got them in and could immediately feel a difference in quality between them and previous pairs I've purchased from other companies. The sizing is accurate, they hold their shape really well throughout the day and do a great job of feeling sturdy and secure. I've tried others before that are marketed as being "buttery soft" and whatever, and they are useless if you are someone that needs a pair to actually feel like something you would be comfortable walking outside of your house in. They don't stretch and sheer out across the butt and they aren't so thin that they show whatever you are wearing underneath. After wearing and washing once, I came back and bought another pair right away.

I would buy them again at full price. I'm 5'10" and the length on these is fine, not too short at all. A size 16/18 in pants and an XL fit. They are a bit tight (which is my fault) but they still fit. If they had a size up, I would buy them again in that size, but the current size does work well enough for me.

title: Just as expected
text:
*UPDATE* I've washed these twice and they have gone crappy. Pilled up like crazy, fabric isn't opaque at all. Like bad enough that you can't wear these in public. And this isn't a matter of being delusional about my size and trying to stuff my body into too small clothes. These are plus size leggings and the fabric is just bad and not thick enough. These are fine still to wear around the house or for layering under jeans since they fit close enough, but that's about it really. Knocking the rating down to 3 stars from 5.

--These are exactly what I was wanting. I'm 5'10" and a size 16/18 and they fit well. Have a big butt and thighs but they still fit well enough to be relatively high waisted on me, they are high enough to help smooth out a baby gut at least. They are long enough for me as well. The fabric is thick and feels comfortable to wear under a long top since it helps to smooth things out. If these wash well, I'm going to buy a few more pairs for sure. My one complaint is that I wish the fabric was just a bit thicker so it was a tiny bit more opaque. But they are fine right now. If they shrink or don't wash well, then I will update the review.

title: If they were a thicker fabric, I'd be happy.
text:
I'm 5'10" and a size 16/18, this review is from someone who doesn't have much experience wearing leggings as pants, so my standards of what I feel comfortable in are pretty high.

Pros: these did fit, they were long enough on me which I was surprised by. I'm not sure if there would be any shrinkage after washing because I am returning these. The fabric was pretty soft and relatively opaque. No hanging strings, holes, etc... good enough quality for the price.
Cons: the fabric is too thin for me to feel comfortable enough in to wear out in public personally. Now this is due to the fact that I've got a big butt and thighs, and these offer zero control or smoothing really. They don't advertise to be smoothing/slimming/control etc... so this isn't exactly a complaint against the product, it is just the reason that I am returning them. Even with a long top on that covers my backside, I still feel kind of exposed in these.
If I had a use for them, these would be great for layering on a cold day, they are smooth and thin enough to fit under jeans, or I would be fine with bumming around the house in them. But that isn't why I bought them.

title: Cute shoes, runs narrow though.
text: I love the color and got a great price in my size, but something about New Balance shoes always has them run super narrow on me. I can wear a size 11-11.5 normally in other shoes, I ordered this in a 12B (was cheaper than smaller size) and they are really tight. I think I can stretch them out though and I like the style and color enough to want to make them work. If you have relatively wide feet though, I would consider that when choosing your size.

title: Nice suit, accurate sizing
text: I will rank this 5 stars because the sizing was accurate and it looked just like the picture. I am returning it though, I just didn't like how it looked on my body. I ordered my clothing size in this and it was pretty spot on. I'm typically an XL top and 16 in pants. The bottoms especially fit great and came up high enough to contain that lower belly pooch and were comfortable. My one complaint would be that the bust runs a tiinnny bit small, in my opinion. It would have been fine if I kept it but just a bit tight. I'm a 38C/40D (depending on my current weight) and it fit and I was contained well, but I would be hesitant if your chest is larger than that.

title: Beautiful suit
text: I took a chance on ordering this suit because there were no reviews yet on the sizing and quality, but it ended up great. We all know how swimsuit sizing can go when ordering online, but this one was spot on. I'm 5'10" and right at a size 16 and the length was just fine. The color matched the picture as well. I am going to be returning it though, the style in the picture is pretty but it just isn't my style. Plus I ordered another one at the same time that makes me look smaller (if I'm being honest with myself) that I like just as well. If I swam more or wasn't working on trying to lose weight, then I would have kept this one too though.

title: Love these.
text:
Due to the great price I found in my size, I ended up buying three pairs of these shoes. I returned one, that was just due to me not liking the look of black patent on them though. I kept the pairs I ordered in blue and white though to go with spring and summer dresses and skirts that I have, trying to dress up my wardrobe a bit so I dont rely on flip flops all the time.

I rank these as running somewhat small, but not terribly so. I am about an 11.5 in shoes, kind of wide. I bought these in a 12 because they were available (which is not super common for this size) and I didn't want the issue of my toes possibly going over the front (not a cute look), and I'm glad I did because they fit perfectly for me. So I would say maybe go half a size up and order direct from Amazon or a seller that has free returns so you can easily send back if the sizing doesn't work out for you.

My one negative, and this is due to my weird toes more than anything, is that my second to last toe has a habit of poking out the side of one of the straps. But not a big deal .

I haven't worn these for an extended period of time, but then I typically don't wear dressy shoes for long. I just don't have many occasions that call for it. But for the short amounts of time that I have worn them, they've been pretty comfortable for me.

title: Nice flats
text: Not much to say about these, they are nude flats. The sizing is very accurate and I got them for a great price. If I wore flats more often, then I wouldn't hesitate to come back and get these in other colors. My one negative is that in the picture, the nude shade has a bit of a pinky tone to it. But in real life, it leans more warm, has more of a yellowish tone. Not a big deal, its just one of those issues that comes up with buying a nude shade like this and the differences in computer screens. They still work for what I need them for.

title: Works, but some concerns about sizing
text:
For reference, I am 5'10" and currently a size 16, a 38C cup. I bought this in a 2x and it just barely fits me. Well I should clarify, it does not fit me like it should, but I can make it work for what I need it for.

If you are above average height or have a long torso, I would be wary of this, its runs kind of short. I have to yank it up to get it to come high enough for me to cover my bust, and even then it still isn't quite high enough to look great at the top. I bought it for a wedding dress though that has a pretty structured top with cups built in, so it wasn't going to be an issue for me. But for others, it definitely would. I agree with others that say the cups run small also. I spill out the sides of it.

Now for the positive, this really sucks you in. Without it, I have a small amount of extra fabric along the waistline of the dress. With it, it almost works too well for me, I would say I have about 3-4 inches of loose fabric now. Like it borders on making me wish I had the extra time to see if I could get the dress taken in a bit, it works that well. With the way that this bodysuit is designed, it really helps to pull me in right at my natural waistline and does a nice job of smoothing in other places. I just wish I could get it in a size up to possibly rectify the length issue.

title: Great ring, especially for the price
text: This ring is beautiful. Great amount of sparkle without seeming like its too much. The texture of it isn't super rough, doesn't snag on fabric. I ordered 4 different titanium and tungsten carbide bands and this is the one I chose to keep.

title: No white background! It’s clear!
text: I bought this bc I thought it had the nice white background. Turns out it’s clear & since my phone is blue it doesn’t look anything like this.  If I had known that I would have purchased something else. It works ok.

title: Awesome!  Great price!  Works well!
text: Perfect. How pissed am I that I recently paid $20 for 1 Fitbit cable and promptly lost the damned thing?  Extremely pissed!  I keep the spare in my medicine bag so hopefully I won’t lose it and my grandson can’t get to it and try to use it as a belt or a dog leash or any of the other nutty things he’s been using the other one for.

title: Worked but took an hour to install
text:
Overall very happy with the end result. If you hate puzzles don’t do it. I love puzzles and it worked for me. Took a lot of concentration and attention to detail and about an hour! The YouTube video helped a ton with installing the new screen. Highly recommend using a how to video when replacing your screen. The tools and supplies they provided were adequate. I did use additional tools from my home to successfully installed a new screen. My screws on the inside of the iPhone were stuck and I had to use an X-Acto knife to get them to come out. The glass Screen for the iPhone was beautiful and worked great. The screen protector that was additional came cracked (Not a big deal as it was extra in my eyes). I did need to use the X-Acto knife to cut off part of a plastic piece to make the final fit. So yes I modified the screen and instructions but ended up working great for me.

title: Two words: "good" but "overpriced"
text:
This is an update AFTER I have purchased the honor 8 (with a heavy discount from manufacturer)

Everything else is as most people have observed: quality build, smooth, ample memory ...

However, one BIG complaint I have is the dual sim - Huawei's own manual (on model FRD-L04) says it CAN be used as dual-sim (or one sim and one sd card), numerous reviews said it support dual-sim, but it doesn't from what I can tell.

why Huawei doesn't support more LTE bands, just like they do on Mate 9??

Another issue is with dual camera - the wide aperture is a great misnomer, wide aperture on smart phone won't give you the bokeh effect, iphone's "portrait" mode is much easier on usability.

---

I bought Honor 5x as soon as it was out on Amazon: it was a good value proposition at the time. Not so for Honor 8.

Honor 8 - I have hands-on experience, it is a step-up from Honor 5x, but not a $200 or double-priced step up.
Most folks who bought the Huawei phone are not because it is really better than iPhone at half the price (though I am sure Huawei wants you to think that way). Yes, it is beautifully designed, and I like 5.2 form factor more than 5.5. The dual camera is nice - but it is not pulling ahead of either iPhone or Samsung. All in all, a good step-up from Honor 5x released in US. That comes to my second point - it is an overpriced phone.

The same phone or other similarly configured phone (from Xiaomi, Le2 etc) will cost about $50 to $100 less, which is significant in this price range. Huawei set this price simply because they can (and a bit greedy since this is US market). No other its fellow competitors from home have released their phones in the US, yet. There maybe some pride on Huawei's part on about its reputation and quality that they think worth the extra. This is not so in my mind: I haven't seen any phone other than iPhone that can enjoy software update for more than 3 years, and hardware can withstand it. Given my experience with Honor 5x, Huawei is no exception either. The bottom line is, I think this is over-priced phone, a bit over 300 or even 350 would have made its name and be more competitive.

title: Bad at most things, but a great phone for the price.
text:
This phone is cheap. It runs an ancient version of Android, can barely run an app and make a phone call at the same time, and is losing compatibility with some basic apps that I used to use every day (e.g. banking). On top of all of this, the sound quality is fair at best, and you can't run bluetooth and wifi at the same time without them interfering with each other (they sit on the same chip).

Despite all of the negative remarks above, I have had this phone for 3 years. 3 years! I've never had a phone last that long, let alone one I bought for $60 with no contract. It takes a beating, and still delivers in some key areas:

First, the battery. This battery is insane (probably because the processor is so weak it doesn't draw any power...). I can forget to charge the phone overnight, and I'll still have a charge the next afternoon.

Second, the durability. I have dropped this phone more times than I can count. Heck, I've even thrown it against the wall to prove a point to gloating iPhone owners. In spite of all that, it keeps ticking. Small cracks on the back cover are the only sign of wear. With the beating I give it, I would expect it to look like Humpty Dumpty (post-fall).

Lastly, size. This phone is very small for a smart phone. It's so cheap I don't bother with a case, and it fits very easily in a hand or pocket.

To summarize:

This is a great cheap phone. In spite of all of its shortcomings, it can call, text, and send emails. It can even load simple web pages (good luck if there are ads though...). If you just want a sturdy little phone that will get you through the day and then some, this is a fine choice. If you have this phone (Note 8), you know that the glass is curved on the edges, so it is difficult to find a screen protector that doesn't provide full coverage and doesn't go around the curved edges.  The problem with a full coverage glass protector is that just about any case that you try needs to press against the sides of the glass to hold the phone properly.  That creates a problem because the pressure of a case on the sides raises the protector off the surface of the glass.  With this case, you don't absolutely need a screen protector, as you have protection once the case is closed.  I have tried two other cases and so far I like this the best of the three. title: Very rigid cover; good quality; partially works on earlier Stylo phone
text: I ordered this for my LG G Stylo phone, but it was designed for a Stylo 2, which is apparently just slightly different.  It does fit my phone, but it partially covers the camera flash and completely covers the laser detection auto focus. I believe it also covers the headphone jack. All the other holes line up okay (microphone, charging port, speaker and hole for the stylus).  All the front openings are available because this is a one-sided case.  If you don't use the camera that much or the headphone jack (which I don't), you could make it work.  It is very rigid, so it seems as if it would be very durable and long lasting.  Because it is a completely rigid case, it was a little difficult to slip the phone into it and I may have cracked the back cover of the phone (the battery cover).  It's possible that it was already cracked from dropping the phone a few times, but I know I made several of the cracks worse putting it in the case and then removing the case.  When I first removed the case, it pulled the back off the phone, in fact.  Possibly the fit might not be quite as tight on a Stylo 2, but if it was not a good firm fit, the case would not stay in place.  My suggestion - once you have it in the case, don't remove it, unless you have to in order to get to the battery or memory card inside your phone.  The only thing that I really didn't like is that this is a one sided case that covers only the back, ends and side of the phone but not the front.  My current case has a cover, to cover the front of the phone as well, so it protects it much better.  My attempts to fit this case to a phone that it wasn't quite designed for should not impact your decision to buy this case.  All I would say is to just be careful inserting it into the case, so as not to flex the phone at all, which might crack the back phone cover (the battery cover) as it did mine.  I wasn't keen on the pink color, but you can order this in other colors.

title: Great-looking case that complements your iPhone 6
text:
I preordered mine and received it on Sept. 19, the same day my iPhone 6 arrived. The color (I chose champagne / champagne) matches the phone perfectly. The case is very light with a sleek profile that makes you forget it's a case at all. Finishing is excellent; there are no rough seams, corners, or edges. After reading that several people had issues with Elago Outfit cases scratching their iPhone 5, I left the protective film on the back of my phone just in case, but don't plan on removing this case until I trade my phone in in a year or two.

At first, I was worried that the thin plastic around the volume / power button might crack, but I've been using it for a month and it is as sturdy as the day I put it on the phone. There is also supposed to be a special coating that repels dirt and fingerprints, and I've been setting my phone down on multiple surfaces and it looks brand-new. If you see smudges / fingerprints on the aluminum panel, simply wipe down with a soft cloth and you're good to go.

The one design feature I'm not crazy about is the fact that the top is left open; the bottom gives plenty of access to the speaker, headphone jack and adapter, and clearly Elago knew the power button had shifted from the top to the right, so I'm a bit confused why the top edge was left completely unprotected, as it seems likely that this is the surface that will hit first when dropped. The case does have a slight lip on the front, so you can set your phone face-down without worries about scratching the screen, but having the top edge enclosed would have made this a great case (so far the phone hasn't gotten scratched on the exposed edge, but I've been pretty careful with it).

Things I like:
+ The case is made in Korea, not China.
+ Elago wrote a follow-up e-mail to ask how I liked my purchase.
+ Elago included several free gifts (a screen protector, cleaning cloth, and a car charger adapter) and a thank you note!
+ Smooth finishing (edges, corners, inside) means less chance of scratching your phone

Things I'd improve:
- Enclose the top edge; since there are no buttons / jacks on top anymore, I can't see a reason for leaving the top edge of your phone / screen exposed to drops / cracks / scratches.

Otherwise this is an excellent case and I would definitely recommend it!

title: �Bend It Like Beckham� a riot of laughs, drama and football.
text:
A friend in London (England, not Ontario) convinced me that I had to see "Bend It Like Beckham," (along with praise from Sundance and the Toronto Film Festival) so lo and behold, one dreary spring day I stepped into a surprisingly crowded theatre (I wasn't sure of a British comedy's marketability in North America). "BILB" proved every bit as wonderful as my friend said, and in a nutshell is a sort of cross between "Monsoon Wedding" and "My Big Fat Greek Wedding."
Jess, a Londoner of Asian descent, plays football in secret since her parents strictly forbid it and want her to grow into a nice, traditional Sikh girl who can cook a full Punjabi dinner. Jess, however, has other plans. She teams up with Jules (short for Juliet), a fellow footballer, and the team coach Joe and an American scout eagerly appraises the two. Along the way Jess has to survive her sister's frantic, bipolar engagement and wedding, come clean to her parents about her joining the team, fights over her blossoming romance, and learns to follow her heart. Jess confides her worries to her David Beckham poster that hangs over her bed. Her room is filled with Beckham memorabilia. Jules' mother is similarly against her daughter playing football, convinced that she must be a lesbian since she favours sports bras, has short hair and wears boyish clothes. The two girls hang out often, finding more similarities than differences, but when Jess nearly kisses Joe, Jules is furious, having eyed him for herself, and a stony rivalry ensues.
The film is doused with Indian culture, including saris, salwar kameez, samosas, Bollywood musicals, singing game shows, bhangra rock, and more, but always finds a more or less comfortable balance between Indian and London cultures. The unbelievably colourful, extravagant wedding was one of my favourite highlights of the film since I adore bhangra rock and Bollywood. The soundtrack is similarly influenced, with many Indian pop songs, and my favourite of all, "The Power of Love" cover (Sitam version) by Amar. The cinematography is at times used for comedic effect, as in rapid cutaways to see the dazed/shocked/delighted expression of parents and relatives, in dizzying, rapid-fire football matches, the colourful exuberance of the Indian wedding, the sizzling energy of a German nightclub, and at times timed shots to capture the beauty of day turning into dusk.
The movie is blessed with a strong cast, a great story, and characters that draw you into their worlds, worries, and triumphs, not to mention a catchy soundtrack, great football action, and a tender romance. "Bend It Like Beckham" will certainly join my other honoured favourites such as "Monsoon Wedding" and "My Big Fat Greek Wedding." Oh, and look for a "There's Something About Mary"-like singalong/bloopers during the credits. If you love football, romantic comedies, and/or Indian culture, you will surely score with "Bend It Like Beckham."
